Countries legally obliged to consider slavery reparations, says UN committee
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
11:54:16 UTC
20:54:16 KST

A UN committee has said countries are legally obliged to consider reparations for the transatlantic slave trade and take other measures to address the enduring legacy of racial discrimination.
Guidance published on Monday by the committee on the elimination of racial discrimination (CERD) said the obligations arose from a legally binding 1965 convention on racial discrimination, not from the legal standards that existed when the slave trade took place.
The committee described the approach as a “paradigm shift” away from debates over historical responsibility that have often been used by governments to resist reparations claims.
“States parties must implement comprehensive reparatory measures for people of African descent, covering all aspects of remedies,” said the UN document, which may be cited in courtrooms.
At least 12.5 million Africans were taken and sold between the 15th and 19th centuries in what CERD called the largest forced displacement in history.
Calls for reparations – ranging from official apologies to financial compensation – have gained momentum internationally, though opponents argue states and institutions should not be held responsible for historical crimes. The EU and Britain abstained from a UN resolution on slavery in March.
Some states have sought to dodge claims for justice in courtrooms by arguing that there were no international laws outlawing the slave trade at the time – the so-called intertemporality principle.
But the UN document argues that, regardless of whether slavery and the slave trade were illegal under the laws of the day, countries remain responsible under current international obligations to tackle their continuing effects.
“Irrespective of the legal characterisation of the original historical acts, states parties remain bound by their present obligations under the convention to address structural inequalities,” the UN document says.
Financial compensation alone is not sufficient, it adds, urging “transformative” measures including opening archives, revising public memorials and establishing independent truth commissions.
Pela Boker Wilson, a committee expert from Liberia who helped draft the document, said she expected states to move beyond broad expressions of regret and review policies and laws.
“We are calling on state parties to take concrete and meaningful action,” she told Reuters. “We want to affirm the dignity of those whose suffering was denied, whose suffering was minimised or forgotten.”

'No jurisdiction': India rejects 'illegal' Court of Arbitration's Indus Waters Treaty award
Edited by: Rohitashwa Ranjan / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 31, 2026, 18:46 IST
Comments

Text Size
Small

MEA said that the Indus Water Treaty will remain in abeyance
NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs on Monday categorically rejected a ruling by World Bank-constituted Court of Arbitration on Indus Water Treaty, terming it an "illegally constituted" organisation.In a statement, MEA said that New Delhi's decision to put the water treaty with Pakistan in abeyance "will remain in force.""This so-called Court was constituted by the World Bank in patent breach of the terms of the Treaty and India categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body," the ministry said."India has never recognised the existence in law of this illegally-constituted and so-called Court of Arbitration, and has consistently maintained that the very establishment of this alleged arbitral body constitutes a grave violation of the Indus Waters Treaty. Accordingly, India has never appeared before this body and has refused to take any cognisance of its earlier pronouncements," it added.
Also read: 'India could use water as weapon': Pakistan minister as Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyanceThe ministry also said that the Court of Arbitration has no "jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions.""Its pronouncements, now or in the future, will have no effect on India’s actions in connection with the projects being undertaken by India," MEA said.
This comes hours after the Court of Arbitration said that the grounds on which India decided to put the Indus Water Treaty in abeyance did not “justify suspension or termination.”
“Accordingly, the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force, and India must observe its obligations under the Treaty,” the court saidNew Delhi put the agreement in abeyance following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year.Since then, Pakistani leaders have repeatedly called water their “red line” and threatened India over the move, describing it as an “act of war.”

Kyiv under near-constant air raid alerts for 5th day as Russian strikes kill 7, injure 43 across Ukraine
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
11:51:00 UTC
20:51:00 KST

Kyiv under near-constant air raid alerts for 5th day as Russian strikes kill 7, injure 43 across Ukraine
Key developments:
- Russia has continued attacking Ukrainian cities for a fifth consecutive day, relying primarily on jet-powered drones, with Kyiv and the surrounding region among the main targets.
- Seven people were killed and another 43 injured across six oblasts over the past day, according to local authorities.
- Russian forces launched 121 long-range attack drones overnight, with Ukrainian air defenses intercepting 96, or roughly 79% of the total.
Ukraine is facing a fifth consecutive day of nonstop Russian jet-powered drone attacks, while Russian strikes in other regions have killed at least seven people and injured another 43 over the past day, local authorities said.
Russian forces have shifted their airstrike tactics in recent days. Rather than launching massive overnight barrages of ballistic and cruise missiles preceded by waves of drones, Moscow is now launching jet-powered drones in separate, near-hourly attacks throughout the day, triggering continuous air raid alerts across Ukrainian cities.
Russia has launched nearly 800 jet-powered drones toward Ukraine over the past four days, as the Aug. 31 attack continues. The drones can reach speeds of up to 600 kph (373 mph), making them roughly four times faster than earlier Russian Shahed-type models.
Kyiv and the surrounding region remain key targets of the strikes, with eight air raid alerts sounding by 1:30 p.m. on Aug. 31. The capital recorded 13 alerts on Aug. 28 — the highest number since Russia launched its full-scale invasion. Constant air raid alerts are disrupting businesses and public transportation, affecting both residents' daily lives and the broader economy.
At the same time, the nonstop attacks are placing mounting strain on Ukraine's air defenses, while also increasing the civilian casualty toll. The continued strikes targeting Kyiv on Aug. 31 injured six people, three of whom were hospitalized in serious condition. Most of the victims were in Pohreby, a village about two kilometers (1.2 miles) north of the capital, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. 
Tymur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv Oblast State Administration, said Russian drones damaged warehouses and a retail outlet in Kyiv Oblast's Brovary district, while three warehouses and a residential building were damaged in the Boryspil district.
Russian forces attacked Ukraine overnight with one Kh-59 cruise missile and 121 long-range attack drones, of which air defenses intercepted 96, the Air Force said. The missile did not reach its target, while several drones evaded air defenses and struck 11 locations. Falling debris was also reported at eight other sites, according to the Air Force.
In eastern Donetsk Oblast, four people were killed and seven injured in Russian strikes in the region over the past day, governor Vadym Filashkin said.
In southeastern Zaporizhzhia Oblast, two people were killed, and three were injured by Russian attacks, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said.
In southern Kherson Oblast, Russian attacks in the region killed one person and injured 16 others, regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin said.
Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast injured five people over the past day, governor Oleksandr Hanzha reported, according to the reports published on Aug. 30 and Aug. 31.
In a separate attack on an industrial facility in the city of Kryvyi Rih in the morning of Aug. 31, a fire broke out at the facility, injuring two men, Hanzha added.
In northeastern Kharkiv Oblast, over the past day, four people were injured, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said.
In southern Odesa Oblast, Russian forces struck Ukrainian postal giant Nova Poshta's terminal on Aug. 31, Odesa Oblast Governor Oleh Kiper said. No civilians were injured, Kiper added.
July of 2026 saw the most civilians killed or injured in Ukraine since March 2022, according to the U.N. Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU).
At least 437 civilians in Ukraine were killed and 2,610 injured in July alone, the monitoring group said on Aug. 13. This represents a 30% increase from June, which previously held the record for the deadliest month since April 2022.
Ukrainian civilian casualties in July 2026 were 70% higher than in July the previous year, while casualties among children also rose to their highest level since April 2022, with 17 children killed and 166 injured.

Rome had already suspended the arrangement with Madrid for a month beginning on July 31, in response to an influx of migrants who crossed into the Spanish territory of Ceuta.
The incident, in which dozens of migrants died, triggered a massive European Union migration emergency and brought Spain's leftist government much criticism, including from Italy.
What else do we know about Italy's extension?
Italy's Interior Ministry said the decision to extend the suspension was taken "due to the persistence of the factors that had led to the reintroduction of the measures on Aug. 1," without clarifying.
The ministry added that Italy was aware of "the steps already undertaken by Spain, together with the European Union, to help bring the situation in the area back to normal in the near future."
The announcement came despite the fact that nearly all of the some 70,000 people who had broken through the barrier returned to Morocco in the days after the incident.
Spain had responded to Italy's suspension by introducing its own border controls for passengers arriving from Italy and on Monday reportedly said it was extending this measure by 15 days, in an apparent tit-for-tat move.
Sanchez says Ceuta incident traced to Russian, Israeli agents
Socialist Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Monday that an "international far-right movement" with "links to Russia and Israel" had created a disinformation campaign on social media that led to the incident at the border fence in Ceuta.
Both Rabat and Madrid had earlier said that the crisis was exacerbated by incorrect information circulating on social media regarding a recent Supreme Court ruling.
"What we know so far is that a ruling by the Supreme Court of July 8 was distorted, which was spread on social networks through fake news, disinformation and also by criminal organizations that traffic in people," Sanchez told broadcaster SER on Monday.
He said there had been a concerted effort "to attack and divide not only Spain but also Europe," without providing further details.
Sanchez added that there was no evidence that Moroccan authorities had been responsible.
Some 5,000 migrants remain in Ceuta, Sanchez said, with at least 1,200 being minors.
On Friday, Spain asked for help from the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) in processing the remaining migrants, amid rising protests against their presence by residents of the exclave.
Ceuta is bordered by Morocco on one side and the sea on the other, with no direct access to the mainland of the European Union, making it difficult for any asylum seekers to access the bloc from there.

Breadcrumb
Israel and Greece sign a multi-billion-dollar weapons deal, the largest between the countries
Israel signed a multi-billion-dollar weapons deal with Greece, the largest between the two Mediterranean countries, as Israeli defense exports soar despite its genocide of Gaza and wars across the region.
Israel's Defense Ministry said Monday the nearly 3 billion Euro ($3.5 billion) defense export deal, coined "Achilles Shield", is one of the country's largest and includes a multilayered air defense system for Greece using Israeli technology.
“Israel and Greece share common strategic interests and face shared regional challenges. At a time when actors with hegemonic ambitions are seeking to expand their influence and undermine stability in the region,” said Defense Minister Israel Katz.
The agreement comes as Israeli weapons exports have reached record highs with more than $19 billion last year, a 30% increase from 2024, according to official data, despite widespread criticism of Israel’s genocide of Gaza, wars with Hezbollah in Lebanon, expanding to fighting with Iran.
Experts say governments look to Israel because its weapons are "battle-tested" and they’re able to see in real time that the munitions and systems work, despite the war crimes and crimes against humanity.
Israel and Greece have deepened defense ties in the last decade. Monday’s signing, however, marks the most significant deal between the two as Greece focuses on modernising its armed forces to keep pace with its neighbor and fellow NATO member Turkey amid long-standing disputes over sea boundaries in the eastern Mediterranean.
Previous deals have included a $1.65 billion agreement with Israeli defense contractor Elbit to build a flight training school in southern Greece as well as the planned sale of Israeli rocket launchers, anti‑tank guided missiles and drones.
Israel says Monday's agreement is the first time it will provide a complete array of defense weapons against a range of threats from ballistic missiles to drones. It includes multiple Israeli systems such as David Sling and SPYDER as well as a new national command and control system. In addition to the agreement, a complementary deal valued at $30 million (26 million Euros) was signed for the sale of Rafael's Drone Dome systems, it said.
“Modern conflicts have already altered the parameters of military defense and deterrence,” Greece’s Defense Minister Nikos Dendias said in a statement after the agreement was signed. “Technology, ballistic missiles, satellite communications, unmanned systems, cyber threats, hybrid forms of warfare and the interconnection of fields of operations have long rendered preexisting defense doctrines completely unrealistic,” he said.
More than half of the Israeli arms industry’s sales are for missiles, rockets and air-defense systems.
For the first time, Israel has surpassed the United Kingdom in its share of global arms exports, making it the world’s seventh-biggest supplier, according to a March report by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.

Russia used five times as many jet-powered drones in July as in June
A Ukrainian military official has said Russia used five times as many jet-powered drones to attack Ukraine in July as it did in June, following a change in its drone attack tactics and increased use of jet-powered UAVs, which are more difficult for the Ukrainian Air Force to shoot down.
Source: Yurii Ihnat, spokesperson for the Ukrainian Air Force, in an interview on the national joint 24/7 newscast
Quote: "The enemy has changed the weapons it uses more than its tactics. In other words, it has significantly increased the number of jet-powered [drones – ed.] specifically. This happened... in July. The enemy used five times as many jet-powered UAVs in July as in June. That was the month when the number of these UAVs, along with Banderol missile drones, began to increase significantly."
Details: Ihnat reported that Russia had launched more than 1,500 UAVs on Ukraine over the past four days. Of these, 800 – more than half – were jet-powered.
Ihnat said the Russians have resorted to using jet-powered drones as Ukraine's defence forces were successfully shooting down and jamming large numbers of conventional petrol-powered Shaheds.
"Of course, they did not start using jet-powered UAVs just recently, but they have now increased their use, realising that they cannot be shot down using the conventional methods we already employ against ordinary UAVs," the spokesperson said.
He added that Ukraine's interception rate for jet-powered UAVs is currently lower than for conventional drones, 88-90% of which are shot down.
Ihnat explained that the successful interception of jet-powered drones requires the use of ground-based air defence systems, aviation systems and platforms, fighter jets equipped with air-to-air missiles, and other weapons.

Andy Burnham should call a cross-party meeting to discuss the UK’s response to worsening extreme weather, including the forthcoming ‘super El Niño’, the Liberal Democrats have said.

Pippa Heylings, the Lib Dem spokesperson for energy security and net zero, said: “Andy Burnham has shown he is able to commit to talking about things people care about, which is good. But there’s been a baffling silence from him on extreme heat. What we have heard so far has been underwhelming. Banning disposable barbecues is good, but we need to see more.”
Heylings and Ed Davey, the Lib Dem leader, wrote to Burnham a fortnight ago, proposing a meeting of the UK’s party leaders “to discuss the long-term measures needed to protect our country from climate impacts and build resilience to the extreme weather we are already experiencing”. They say they have not had a response.
Heylings contrasted Burnham’s reluctance to address the climate crisis with his prioritising of social care, on which he has called for cross-party support: “We want the same approach [to the climate].”
She said even the leaders of Reform and the Conservatives, both of whom have vowed to scrap net zero and downplayed the climate crisis, should be able to join in an effort to protect the UK. “I think there is not a single MP who would not want to show their constituents they were trying to prepare us [for the impacts of extreme weather],” she said.
The forthcoming El Niño could bring more serious problems, Heylings said. “The scale of this Super El Niño is unprecedented and will have impacts here in the UK exacerbating our extreme weather particularly with more intense flooding and storms over the autumn and winter. We’re looking at a double whammy.”
Any cross-party approach should not be limited to discussing preparedness for extreme weather, she said. “The key question is how do we stop it worsening?”
Clive Lewis, the Labour MP for Norwich South, backed the Lib Dem call for a cross-party meeting. “It’s the kind of politics we need,” he said. “We may disagree on how we do it and how far we go, but political cooperation like this is the start of consensus building, something any radical transition has to build across both political parties and society, especially if they’re to take on those vested interests that want the status quo to continue.”
But Jon Pearce, the Labour MP for High Peak in Derbyshire, warned it was unlikely a meeting would happen.
“The idea the Conservatives and Reform UK would be willing to face up to the risks we face is for the birds,” he said. “The Conservatives and Reform UK have ripped up the political consensus on tackling climate change as they compete to see who can most downplay the need for action.
“They are refusing to see what is right in front of their eyes: wildfires, drought, pressure on water supplies and farmers facing growing challenges on food production. There should be political consensus on a matter of such national importance but sadly there is not.”
In the past few years, Reform and the Conservatives have broken sharply with the consensus on the need for climate action, despite polls consistently showing a large majority of voters support the idea.
A spokesperson for the Conservatives said: “We wouldn’t speculate on hypothetical talks to which we have not been invited.”
The Reform party did not respond to a request for comment.
Hannah Spencer, a Green party MP, said: “The climate crisis should be a priority across every sector of the economy and every government department. Greens have led this agenda for decades and welcome the consistently strong support shown by voters for all parties for bold climate action.”
A spokesperson for the government said: “The UK continues to be a world leader in tackling the climate crisis, accelerating the transition to clean power, and acting to protect people and places from the impacts of climate change that are already being felt across the country.
“We are working to adapt to the changing climate through our work with the National Drought Group, building nine new reservoirs across the country and investing at least £10.5bn by March 2036 to construct new flood and coastal erosion schemes, as extreme weather becomes more frequent.”

World Central Kitchen chief slams IDF soldier behind Zomi Frankcom attack
In short:
World Central Kitchen's chief José Andrés has hit back at an Israeli commander who defended the decision to strike a convoy that killed Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom.
He released the video after an ABC interview with Israeli colonel Nochi Mendel, who ordered the 2024 drone strike that killed Ms Frankcom and six of her colleagues in Gaza.
What's next?
The WCK chief has also renewed calls for an independent investigation into the April 2024 attack.
World Central Kitchen has hit back at an Israeli commander who defended the decision to strike a convoy that killed seven aid workers, including Australian Zomi Frankcom, saying "we will never accept the death of humanitarian workers".
In a video on X, the organisation's chief José Andrés said there was "never an excuse for killing" humanitarians.
He released the video in response to an ABC interview with Israeli colonel Nochi Mendel, who ordered the deadly drone strike on an aid convoy in Gaza that killed Ms Frankcom, along with six of her colleagues, in April 2024.
Colonel Mendel told the ABC he did not intend to harm aid workers but said, "I'm not sorry for what I did."
He said he later became aware of what he claims were links between World Central Kitchen (WCK) and Hamas, describing the organisation as not "really a neutral organisation" — allegations the WCK calls "false and outrageous".
A spokesperson for the WCK told the ABC that "this is the latest attempt to shift blame away from the IDF's own actions".
Responding to Colonel Mendel's interview, which was published last week after being conducted in October 2025, Mr Andrés refuted the commander's claims.
"He said we are not a neutral organisation. Really? Let me be very clear to him and to the whole world," he said.
"We are humanitarians."
The organisation also renewed calls for an independent investigation into the April 2024 attack.
Colonel Mendel, the commander who ordered the attack, was sacked from his role as chief of staff for the Israeli military's Nahal infantry brigade.
However, as part of a wider release of military findings on August 19, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it would not pursue a criminal investigation or take additional measures against anyone involved in the incident.
The Frankcom family was "deeply disappointed" by the decision and called for an independent investigation.
"We want an independent investigation, with all the video on audio released in public, so the world can know the truth," Mr Andrés said, echoing Ms Frankcom's family.
"Because we continue to grieve for our friends. We will never forget them or stop fighting for them."
On April 1, 2024, the group was travelling in three armoured cars branded with the WCK logo and driving through part of the Gaza Strip that had been declared a "humanitarian fire control zone" while coordinating movements with the IDF.
An Israeli drone fired three missiles at the convoy — one at each of the cars in succession — as survivors of the initial strike attempted to move from one vehicle to another.
In findings released on August 19 this year, the IDF said it identified a gunman on a truck in the humanitarian aid convoy and believed the situation "corresponded to a scenario in which the Hamas terrorist organisation had taken control of the convoy" and claimed the convoy deviated from the approved route.
In response to the findings, WCK said the IDF had full knowledge that the team was unarmed and was aware of its movement, identities and activities in advance.
"They knew there was no excuse," Mr Andrés reiterated in the video.
"They knew everything about our operations in Gaza in real time. In fact, there were clear orders not to fire on our people."
At the time, the IDF said the attack was a grave mistake, arising from misidentification of the occupants of the convoy as Hamas members.
An Australian investigation into the Israeli government's response to the incident, led by retired defence chief Air Chief Marshal Mark Binskin and published August 2, 2024, found the deaths had been the result of the first vehicle being misidentified due to a number of factors.
They included the presence of armed security in the vicinity, confirmation bias and a "failure within the IDF to fully disseminate and/or read the detailed movement plan approved by the convoy".
As part of the recent release on various IDF investigations into civilian deaths since October 7, the military said it did conclude there were serious failures.
It said the IDF "mistakenly believed that the vehicles contained Hamas military operatives and therefore struck the vehicles", but had stopped short of launching a criminal investigation.
Two IDF commanders — including Colonel Mendel — have already been stripped of their ranks as colonel and major.
A colonel, a major general and a brigadier general have also been reprimanded over the incident.
The ABC's Unravel podcast is investigating the incident, with a report due later this year.

Modi-Putin meeting at SCO: Can India-Russia ties hold?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
11:47:00 UTC
20:47:00 KST

Modi-Putin meeting at SCO: Can India-Russia ties hold?
August 31, 2026
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to meet in Kyrgyzstan's capital, Bishkek, on Monday on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit — a bloc often seen as a counterweight to US influence.
The meeting comes against the backdrop of the fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran, which has disrupted global energy markets, and Russia's war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year.
India has remained engaged with the SCO while resisting efforts to turn it into an anti-Western bloc. Its position reflects a broader effort to maintain relationships with competing powers.
That approach is under greater pressure. Russia remains under Western sanctions over the war in Ukraine. Meanwhile, India has faced US pressure over its purchases of Russian oil, alongside wider trade tensions.
A former Indian ambassador to the US, Meera Shankar, told DW that India's relationship with Russia should not be seen as directed against the US.
"India has a long-standing strategic relationship with Russia. This is not directed against any country but intended to help India meet its national goals," said Shankar.
Energy ties deepen between India, Russia
Energy has become the most visible change in the India-Russia relationship.
Before 2022, when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, it supplied only a small share of India's crude imports. Discounted Russian oil rapidly changed that, making Moscow one of India's biggest suppliers.
It has also become the most contentious part of India's relationship with the US, which has pressed New Delhi to reduce its purchases from Russia. India maintains that securing affordable and reliable energy is a national interest.
The disruption to traditional energy supplies has made that calculation more complicated. This year's US-Israel war on Iran and disruption of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz have affected India's purchases from the Gulf and pushed up prices.
Shankar said India is responding by diversifying its sources of supply, including both Russia and the US.
"In the long run, a transition to a non-fossil fuel economy would strengthen India's energy independence. But this will not happen overnight," she added.
Until then, Shankar said, India will take steps it considers necessary to stabilize supplies and protect its people.
Future of India-Russia defense cooperation
Defense remains the other major pillar, but here the direction of travel is clearer: India's dependence on Russian equipment has been declining.
The Ukraine war has raised questions over Russia's production capacity, delivery schedules and ability to supply spare parts after decades as a major supplier of India's military hardware.
"India remains one of Russia's oldest and largest arms buyers, and perhaps the last major one," Aravind Yelery, an associate professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in the Indian capital, New Delhi, told DW.
"New Delhi is increasingly reluctant to commit to Russia's fifth-generation fighter program and has little appetite for new Russian hardware unless it can be incorporated into India's indigenous production plans," he added.
While India has diversified its purchases, that does not mean the defense relationship is disappearing.
However, the terms are changing, with India looking for a relationship that contributes to its own defense production, so that it can move away from simply buying finished systems.
The China question
Russia's growing dependence on China has also become an unavoidable part of the India-Russia equation.
Since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in early 2022, China has become indispensable to Russia as a market, supplier and economic partner. That has reduced Moscow's ability to serve as a counterweight to Beijing.
Yelery sees an important distinction in the two relationships.
"Strategically, Russia's relationship with China remains structurally transactional, a dependence it can ill afford to compromise, whereas its relationship with India rests on partnership," he said.
India still has reasons to keep Moscow close: energy, defense, access to the Russian market and a longstanding political relationship across Eurasia. But the strategic calculation has changed.
India's 'America plus' strategy
Strategic affairs expert C Raja Mohan said that Russia's growing dependence on China has changed its strategic value for India.
"Russia is no longer in a position to help India balance China," Mohan, a professor of American studies at Jindal Global University, told DW.
This changes India's expectations from the relationship with Russia.
The emphasis is increasingly on specific interests — energy security, defense supplies, trade and access to technology — while India's larger strategic weight increasingly rests on relationships with the US and its allies.
India has expanded defense and technology cooperation with Washington, while deepening ties with partners such as France and Israel.
Mohan describes this approach as an "America plus" strategy, whereby India maintains its partnership with the US while widening its engagement with other major powers.
"India is trying to reduce its exposure to American volatility, but it still recognizes that Washington is its most important partner," he said.
What do Modi and Putin want?
Rajan Kumar, a professor of Russian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, said Putin wants reassurance that India will remain engaged with Moscow despite pressure from Washington.
"President Putin needs an assurance from Prime Minister Modi that India will not ditch Russia when the latter is facing the worst possible crisis after the 1990s," Kumar told DW.
He expects continuity rather than a dramatic reset. "I think it is more about continuation of existing ties amid US pressure," he added.
Energy trade and payment mechanisms, ways to increase Indian exports to Russia, defense cooperation and the two countries' assessments of the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran are likely to remain important.
The bigger test will come in Delhi in September, when Putin is expected to return for the BRICS summit.
The Bishkek meeting can keep the political relationship on track, but the Delhi talks will show whether that political continuity can produce progress on trade, energy, defense and technology.
The relationship is no longer what it was before the Ukraine war. Energy has become far more important, India's defense dependence is being recalibrated, and Russia's closeness to China has altered the strategic equation.
"The relationship has a value that goes beyond individual deals. Putin appears well aware that India carries an independent strategic weight that China's structural leverage cannot substitute," said Yelery.
Edited by: Emmy Sasipornkarn

Russia Drops FAB-500 Bomb on Sloviansk, Destroying Part of Apartment Building, Injuring 4
Russian forces struck an apartment building in Sloviansk, Donetsk region, with a FAB-500 aerial bomb early on August 31, injuring four people and damaging dozens of residential buildings, local authorities reported.
Sloviansk Mayor Vadym Liakh said the Russian airstrike hit the city at around 4:20 a.m., with the impact recorded in the central part of Sloviansk.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The strike destroyed an entire section of a multi-story apartment building from the first through the fifth floor, as well as a private house. At least 32 other apartment buildings, a hotel, a kindergarten, and a vehicle were also damaged, according to the mayor.
The Donetsk Regional Prosecutor’s Office said four residents between the ages of 61 and 66 were injured while inside their homes.
The victims sustained blast-related injuries, bruises, and lacerations and are receiving medical treatment, prosecutors said.
Law enforcement authorities reported that the strike damaged a total of 34 apartment and private residential buildings, as well as six vehicles.
The attack on Sloviansk came amid further Russian strikes elsewhere in Ukraine. In the Bucha district of Kyiv region, at least 38 people were killed and another 20 injured after Russian forces struck an enterprise, triggering a subsequent detonation.
Emergency medical teams provided assistance to all those affected, with seven of the injured requiring hospitalization.

The European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) has decided to uphold the trademark "official hometown of Santa Claus", owned by the city of Rovaniemi in Finnish Lapland.
The EUIPO made its decision after a request was filed to have the trademark cancelled. The agency, however, found that there were no grounds for revoking it.
The "official hometown of Santa Claus" trademark is registered in the EU as well as in the United States, Britain, Japan and Norway, among other countries.
The cancellation request was filed by Dutch freelance journalist Lex Boon.
Boon told Yle in 2025 that he was not trying to take on Santa Claus or the city of Rovaniemi. His argument was simply that, as a fictional character, Santa Claus could have his hometown anywhere.

IN BRIEF: What is known about detention of two Russians working for Ukraine in Crimea

Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
11:45:37 UTC
20:45:37 KST

MOSCOW, August 31. /TASS/. Federal Security Service (FSB) officers have detained in Crimea two Russian nationals who shared data about Russian defense ministry facilities in the peninsula with Ukraine and scouted locations for hiding explosives for use in terror attacks, the FSB press service said.
TASS has summed up what is known at this moment.
Working for Kiev
Unlawful activities of Russian nationals born in 1968 and 1974, who collaborated with Ukrainian special services, were foiled in Crimea, the press service said.
According to the FSB, two Crimean residents were recruited by officers of the Ukrainian army’s special operations force via a popular messenger.
On instructions from one of the officers, they shared data on the location of the Russian foreign ministry’s facilities and movements of military vehicles in the region with the enemy.
They also disseminated pro-Ukrainian nationalist materials on the internet.
Apart from that, they packed caches with makeshift explosive devices to be used to stage terror attacks.
Searches and interrogation
Search operations yielded four makeshift explosive devices stuffed with more than five kilograms of foreign-made explosive substances and a phone containing correspondence with their overseer.
The detainees confessed, as seen in a video released by the FSB.
The detained are a man and a woman.
The woman confessed to taking photos of military vehicles and tracing caches with explosives at the instruction of an officer of Ukrainian special service.
She also photographed drawings with anti-Russian slogans on the backdrop of the St. Nicholas Cathedral in Yevpatoria.
The FSB also released her Ukrainian-language correspondence with the overseer.
The man also confessed to collaborating with a representative of Ukrainian special services.
At his instruction, he traced caches, explosives.
Apart from that, the man took photos of himself holding a notepad containing a drawing with anti-Russian slogans near tourist sites in Yevpatoria.
Criminal case and measures of restriction
Criminal cases were opened against the detainees under article 275 (high treason) and part 3, article 222.2 of the Russian Criminal Code (illegal trafficking of explosive substances and explosive devices).
A court ruled to place them under arrest for two months, the press service of the FSB department for Crimea and Sevastopol told TASS.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on August 31, 2026
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
19:45:01 CST
20:45:01 KST

At the invitation of the government of the Russian Federation, from September 2 to 4, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council Ding Xuexiang will travel to Russia to attend the 11th Eastern Economic Forum and hold the 13th meeting of the China-Russia Investment Cooperation Committee, the 23rd meeting of the China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee, and the 8th China-Russia Energy Business Forum.
Xinhua News Agency: With rescue efforts still underway following the mudslide in Gyirong, could you please provide further details on the progress of rescue work related to foreign countries?
Guo Jiakun: The devastating mudslide, triggered by a sudden glacial collapse in Nepal’s border area, has caused massive casualties and left many unaccounted for in both China and Nepal. While urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts at home, China also immediately reached out to Nepal to support its emergency response and disaster relief. President Xi Jinping sent a condolence message to Nepali President Ram Chandra Poudel. Premier Li Qiang also expressed condolences to the Nepali side. The meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee called for emergency assistance to the affected areas in Nepal and international cooperation in rescue and relief.
On August 29, Foreign Minister Wang Yi spoke with Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal over the phone. He noted that China and Nepal are a community linked by mountains and rivers and a shared future. In the face of the disaster, the two countries should stand firmly together, join hands to overcome the difficulties, and demonstrate the traditional friendship through concrete actions. The Chinese government has provided Nepal with emergency cash assistance and humanitarian aid. The first batch of 50 tons of relief supplies has already arrived in Kathmandu. Two rescue teams composed of Chinese tunnel rescue experts have rushed to the disaster-stricken areas in Nepal. We have also shared with the Nepali side important information such as images, satellite, and hydrological data of the disaster-affected areas, including early-warning information on an upstream barrier lake. China is actively assisting stranded Nepali citizens in returning to Nepal as soon as possible. As of noon yesterday, all Chinese nationals in Nepal’s disaster-hit areas, with whom contact has been reestablished, have been safely relocated.
At present, China is making every effort to search for and rescue those unaccounted for both within the country and abroad. At the same time, we maintain close communication with foreign embassies in China to jointly identify missing foreign nationals and properly handle follow-up matters.
China News Service: To follow up on your announcement about Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang’s trip to Russia to attend the 11th Eastern Economic Forum and hold the 13th meeting of the China-Russia Investment Cooperation Committee, the 23rd meeting of the China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee, and the 8th China-Russia Energy Business Forum, could you share with us the background, program and China’s expectation of the visit?
Guo Jiakun: Themed on “The Far East: Development for the Benefit of People,” the 11th Eastern Economic Forum will be held in Vladivostok, Russia from September 1 to 4. Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang will attend the plenary session of the forum, co-chair the institutionalized meetings of China-Russia Investment Cooperation Committee and China-Russia Energy Cooperation Committee, as well as China-Russia Energy Business Forum with Russian leaders, and hold meetings with them.
This year marks the 30th anniversary of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination, and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. China will take this opportunity to implement the important common understandings of the two heads of state, make greater progress in developing the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era, and bring benefits to the two peoples. China also looks forward to working with various parties to step up communication, enhance mutual trust, stick to openness and cooperation, and share the opportunities of development, so as to make greater contribution to promoting regional revitalization and development as well as the common welfare of the people of all countries.
CGTN: His Majesty King Harald V of Norway passed away. I wonder if China has any comment?
Guo Jiakun: King Harald V was highly esteemed and deeply loved by the Norwegian people. He was committed to promoting China-Norway friendship, paid multiple visits to China and made significant contributions to bilateral exchange and cooperation. China mourns his passing and extends sincere condolences to the royal family, government and people of Norway.
Bloomberg: Some Indian TV channels have blamed China for the floods and mudslide disaster. They say China is going ahead with major construction projects in hydropower and infrastructure. Would the ministry like to comment on this?
Guo Jiakun: We noted that experts and official institutions of China and Nepal have made some assessment on the cause of the disaster. According to their analysis, the mudslide was triggered by a collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal. In the face of tragic disasters, we reject malicious speculation that has no factual basis.
Sky News: It appears that China has censored and taken down some of the more dramatic videos of that terrible flood smashing into Gyirong Port. Can I ask why China has done that? There have been some suggestions that the numbers of missing and dead are being understated. Can I ask what China’s response is to those accusations?
Guo Jiakun: Intensive search, rescue and relief operations are still underway in an orderly manner in the disaster-hit areas. China has been open, transparent and timely in information release. Smear and disinformation is most unwelcome at a time of disaster response.
Shenzhen TV: It is reported that the Third APEC Senior Officials’ Meeting concluded in Dalian on August 28. Could you brief us on the meeting and its main outcomes?
Guo Jiakun: From August 17 to 28, the Third Senior Officials’ Meeting of APEC China and related meetings were held in Dalian. Deputy Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu attended the meeting and delivered remarks.
This was the largest Senior Officials’ Meeting held during the APEC China Year in terms of both attendance and number of events. During the meeting, APEC committees and working groups held nearly 130 meetings and events, covering areas such as trade, transportation, food, customs, science and technology, energy, health, disaster reduction, and anti-corruption. More than 3,000 representatives from APEC member economies, the APEC Secretariat, and APEC observers attended the meetings.
Participants held in-depth discussions under the theme of APEC China Year and “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together” and around the three priority areas of “Openness, Innovation, and Cooperation”, and focused on comparing notes on the outcomes for the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting to be held in Shenzhen this November.
Under the “Openness” priority, China hosted a policy dialogue on connectivity, laying the groundwork for developing an upgraded APEC Connectivity Blueprint.
Under the “Innovation” priority, China hosted a policy dialogue on the digital economy and artificial intelligence as drivers of economic growth. Participants held in-depth discussions on leveraging AI to promote economic growth, improve people’s well-being, and bridge the digital divide, continuing the positive momentum generated by APEC Digital Week held in Chengdu in July.
Under the “Cooperation” priority, China keeps advancing result‑oriented cooperation covering such areas as anti‑corruption, customs, food security, fisheries and maritime affairs, public health and energy. Major deliverables have been secured on themes such as improving integrity for prosperity and customs cooperation to bolster trade security and facilitation.
The final Senior Officials’ Meeting of the APEC China Year will be held in Shenzhen on the eve of the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting this November. We welcome reporters to continue following and covering events under the APEC China Year.
Reuters: More than 900 people are believed to be stuck inside blocked hydropower project tunnels in Nepal after the flood last week. Were there any Chinese nationals working at these projects and has the government or the ministry identified if any of those Chinese nationals are trapped in the tunnels?
Guo Jiakun: Nearly 100 Chinese nationals are among those missing in Nepal. The Nepali side has been trying every possible means to search for and rescue those missing or trapped. Tunnel experts from China have arrived in the affected area in Nepal to assist in rescue efforts.
Phoenix TV: Japan’s Self-Defense Forces (SDF) in a statement on August 28 said that they had dismissed SDF officer Kodai Murata. The SDF said it is extremely regrettable that one of its members committed such an act, and it will take thorough measures to have its personnel strictly follow laws and regulations. What is China’s comment? Does this address China’s concerns?
Guo Jiakun: It is shockingly malignant for a sitting Japanese SDF officer to break into the Chinese embassy carrying a knife and threaten the Chinese side with violence. This incident seriously violates the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, gravely threatens the safety and security of Chinese diplomatic personnel and premises, and exposes deep-seated problems in Japan, including the rampant spread of right-wing impact and lack of supervision and discipline in the SDF. We noted that Japanese public prosecutors have indicted the person concerned. We urge the Japanese side to earnestly fulfill its duty, bring the perpetrator to account, conduct a thorough investigation and correct the wrongdoings. This is also what the international community hopes to see.
Bloomberg: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the world cannot have a US$1.2 trillion trade surplus with China and he said the G20 countries should reexamine their terms of trade with the country. Would the Foreign Ministry like to comment?
Guo Jiakun: China‑U.S. economic and trade ties are mutually beneficial in nature. China never seeks trade surplus. We oppose unilateral tariff measures in all forms. Committed to high‑standard opening up, China, with its vast market, offers new opportunities to all, including the United States. Both sides need to act on the important common understandings reached between the two presidents, resolve outstanding issues through consultation on the basis of equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit, and strive to maintain the hard‑won positive momentum in bilateral trade.

Has China informed Nepal with unusual signs or early warning indicators before the disaster happened? What measures will China take concerning data sharing with Nepal in the future?

China will continue giving strong support to Nepal in its relief efforts and strengthen cooperation with Nepal on disaster prevention and control for the shared benefit of both peoples.

Guo Jiakun: In the wake of the disaster, the Nepali government has been fully committed to disaster response and relief efforts. The world has reached out to help. The Nepali government’s decisions and requests should be respected, instead of being a target of unwarranted speculation.

China unveils measures to expand, upgrade consumer goods consumption

Unknown Publisher

BEIJING, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- China has unveiled measures to expand and upgrade consumer goods consumption, aiming to bring total retail sales of consumer goods to around 60 trillion yuan (about 8.85 trillion U.S. dollars) by 2030, according to an implementation guideline made public on Monday.
The guideline, jointly issued by seven government departments, including the Ministry of Commerce and the National Development and Reform Commission, calls for fostering 10-trillion-yuan markets in areas such as green, smart and health consumption by 2030.
Retail sales of trillion-yuan product categories, including automobiles, home appliances, communications equipment, textiles and clothing, are also expected to continue growing, with these markets remaining among the world's largest.
The guideline outlines four major tasks to promote goods consumption, namely promoting the consumption of durable goods, improving the quality of everyday consumer goods, supporting consumption of specialty products and fostering demand for upgraded products.
It further specifies measures that include expanding automobile consumption across the entire industrial chain, promoting smart home applications, supporting consumption of products for elderly people and children, and boosting consumption of green, smart and health products. ■

China's space-based computing cloud starts regular in-orbit services
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
19:43:12 CST
20:43:12 KST

BEIJING, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- A China-built space computing cloud has recently started offering regular in-orbit experimental services, according to its developer.
Led by Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (BUPT), the orbital computing power facility automates end-to-end operations across satellite platforms, space servers, ground stations and data centers, giving worldwide users a full life-cycle service from task submission, deployment, execution, monitoring to results delivery.
Space computing refers to an emerging computing paradigm that deploys data processing, storage, intelligent analysis and decision-making capabilities on orbital platforms, such as satellites and space stations.
The Chinese computing cloud platform operates on the Tiansuan Constellation, launched by BUPT in 2021. As the world's first space computing constellation, it has deployed 16 low-Earth-orbit satellites and seven ground stations, supported more than 60 institutions in orbital tests and drawn researchers from more than 50 countries and regions to its ecosystem.
It offers several key technological capabilities, such as building reusable platform-based services, supporting long-term reliable operation of onboard software, and laying a foundation for real-time in-orbit processing of space data and autonomous satellite decision-making.
Since entering service, the platform has supported multiple tasks, including in-orbit big-data computing and 6G communications. More than 100 users have accessed the energy-efficient service, the university said on Sunday.
Compared with ground-based data centers, the advantages of space computing cloud lie in real-time responsiveness and global coverage.
Traditional data centers are constrained by high energy consumption, limited land resources, high cooling costs, and limited coverage, which can hardly meet future demands for ultra-large-scale, green, and globally covered computing power, while space-based computing offers a zero-carbon, sustainable, and widely accessible alternative, said Yu Guobin, deputy director of the commercial space department of the State Administration of Science, Technology and Industry for National Defense, at 2026 Space Computing Industry Conference held in Beijing in April.
The official noted that the space-based computing technology can offer real-time and intelligent services to emergency response, marine observation, aviation and shipping, and polar expeditions.
According to the BUPT, the platform's value lies in helping the space information industry move from hardware delivery to persistent service delivery, cultivating new industrial growth areas in satellite internet, 6G, commercial space and emergency communications. Some of these fields are among the key emerging industries that China aims to foster over the next five years. ■

Chinese-built expressway opens to boost Serbia's economic development: Serbian president

This photo taken on Aug. 30, 2026 shows a view of the Chinese-built Danube Corridor expressway in Pozarevac, Serbia. The Chinese-built Danube Corridor expressway will boost Serbia's economic development, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic said Sunday at the expressway's opening ceremony. The expressway officially opened to traffic on Monday.(Photo by Wang Wei/Xinhua)
POZAREVAC, Serbia, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese-built Danube Corridor expressway will boost Serbia's economic development, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic said Sunday at the expressway's opening ceremony.
Vucic, along with First Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Sinisa Mali, Minister of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure Aleksandra Sofronijevic, and Zhang Zhe, charge d'affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Serbia, attended the event.
After traveling along the Danube Corridor expressway on Sunday, Vucic spoke highly of its significance for Serbia's development, saying that the project will play an important role in advancing Serbia's national interests, boosting domestic tourism and driving economic growth in the country's eastern region.
The expressway would officially open to traffic on Monday, announced Vucic.
Zhang said he believed that the completion of the Danube Corridor would attract an increasing number of tourists to the scenic eastern part of Serbia.
"This also confirms what we often say -- roads connect not only cities with cities, but also the friendship of peoples and opportunities for future development," Zhang said.
According to Shandong Hi-Speed Group, the project's contractor, the Danube Corridor expressway is an important branch of the E75 motorway in Europe and another flagship project of China-Serbia cooperation.
The 68-km expressway has four lanes in both directions and a designed speed of 100 km per hour.
Construction took five years, during which Vucic visited the site seven times and hailed the project as "the road to the future." ■

Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot urged U.S. Ambassador Bill White on Monday to stop targeting government officials in his social media tirades, as further provocation could strain bilateral ties.

Advertisement

Zelenskyy enforces NSDC decision on regional resilience plans
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
14:41:22 EEST
20:41:22 KST

President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has enacted a decision of the National Security and Defense Council (NSDC) regarding the status of implementation of comprehensive resilience plans for individual regions and the approval of the Comprehensive Resilience Plan for the territorial community of the city of Kyiv.
Relevant decree No. 838/2026 was published on the website of the head of state on Monday.
According to the document, control over the implementation of the NSDC decision is assigned to Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine Ihor Klymenko. The decree enters into force on the day of its publication.
The NSDC decision attached to the decree specifically provides for the approval of the Comprehensive Resilience Plan for the territorial community of Kyiv.
In particular, the NSDC instructed Kyiv City State Administration, Kyiv City Mayor, Kyiv City Council, and a number of central government bodies to ensure the unconditional and timely implementation of Kyiv’s resilience plan and to inform the NSDC and the Cabinet of Ministers monthly by the 10th regarding its execution.
The Cabinet of Ministers was instructed to update comprehensive resilience plans taking into account realistic prospects for implementing measures before the start of the heating season, ensure co-financing for the Kyiv plan, and seek additional funding sources, particularly from international partners. The government must also ensure the creation of fuel, equipment, and material reserves, the protection of critical infrastructure facilities, and support for the restoration of Ukrzaliznytsia rolling stock.
Local self-government bodies were instructed to secure a physical fuel reserve for at least two weeks, primarily for life-support facilities, as well as to prepare apartment buildings for autonomous operation by equipping them with independent backup power systems.
Thermal and electric power enterprises must ensure the protection of critical facility elements using first-level technical protection solutions prior to the start of the heating season and create a reserve of equipment, components, and materials for prompt repairs.

The water level of the Rhine has risen in Germany, but shipping remains restricted
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
14:41:16 EEST
20:41:16 KST

The water level of the Rhine has risen in Germany, but shipping remains restricted
Kyiv • UNN
The level of the Rhine near Kaub rose to 72 cm after the rains, but about 1.5 meters is needed for vessels to be fully loaded. By the end of the week, the water level may fall again.
The water level in the Rhine River in Germany has risen sharply after recent rains, but shipping is still difficult. Vessels can already carry more cargo, but the water level still does not allow them to operate at full capacity. Reuters reports, UNN writes.
Details
According to the WSV, on Monday the water level at the gauge station in Kaub, near Koblenz, was about 72 cm, compared with 60 cm on Friday. In mid-August, the level fell below 10 cm — significantly lower than the previous record low of 25 cm recorded in 2018.
For reference
WSV is Germany’s Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration.
Additional information
Despite the improvement, vessels continue to operate with reduced loads. For fully loaded shipping, the water level in Kaub needs to be around 1.5 metres.
Cargo has to be distributed among several vessels, increasing costs for industry. A significant share of freight transport has also been redirected to road and rail.
Rain is forecast this week, but any improvement will depend on how much precipitation actually falls
The WSV forecasts that the water level in the river may fall again toward the end of this week, although it is expected to remain significantly higher than at the beginning of August.
This summer, Germany and other European countries experienced a series of heatwaves and a lack of precipitation, which led to falling water levels on waterways such as the Rhine — an important route for transporting grain, minerals, coal and petroleum products.

Search continues for 18 passengers after ferry capsized in Northern Cyprus
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
12:41:05 BST
20:41:05 KST

'She slipped out of my hand' - couple's children missing after ferry capsizes
- Published
Ayten Bicer felt her 12-year-old daughter slip from her grasp and disappear as the ferry they were travelling on capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday, killing eight people.
Her daughter Miray and six-year-old son Memhet Asaf are among 20 people still missing after the vessel sunk while en route to Turkey from the coastal town of Kyrenia, in the self-proclaimed Turkish republic on Cyprus.
She and her husband, Hayri, survived and, like many other families, are waiting for news of their loved ones back in port as rescuers continue to search.
"She was saying, 'Don't let go'. And I didn't let go of my daughter. I swear, I didn't let her go," Bicer told reporters through tears.
Bicer said a suitcase fell on top of her, which forced her daughter from her grip. She managed to grab hold of her daughter's foot, but her shoes were coated in engine oil from the overturned vessel and she slipped through her hands.
"It was slippery everywhere. It was like oil. She slipped out of my hand," she recalled.
The family was returning to Turkey after a holiday on the Mediterranean island.
"We couldn't intervene, we lost our children," Hayri Bicer said. "Two of my three children are gone. We left them. We are leaving them on this island as we go."
The vessel had been carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members. Nineteen passengers are currently being treated in hospitals in northern Cyprus, local authorities say.
The eight crew members, including the ship's captain, and one other man were formally arrested on Monday. They will be detained for three days, while warrants have been issued for several other people.
The privately owned ferry left the popular holiday resort of Kyrenia at about 12:30 (09:30 GMT), en route to the town of Tasucu in Turkey.
It had been scheduled to travel to Turkey on Saturday but its journey was delayed due to severe storms hitting the island. The seas were still rough on Sunday.
Some eyewitness accounts say the double-hulled ferry jolted violently before slamming onto the sea surface, with part of its bow bursting open on impact.
Ünal Üstel, prime minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), which is only recognised by Turkey, told local media the boat was hit by two waves before it capsized.
While the captain of the vessel was trying to recover from the first wave, a second wave hit and it began taking on water, he said.
The boat has completely sunk and is lying at a depth of 514m (1,686ft), officials say.
Debris remains scattered across the water, including a black wheelie suitcase bobbing on the surface and a sheet of steel that appeared to have broken away from the ferry.
Authorities are attempting to recover the vessel's black box recorder to establish what happened.
A ship will be arriving from Turkey on Tuesday to help with search efforts, TRNC President Tufan Erhurman said.
Meanwhile, a three-day period of national mourning began on Monday.
The ferry - a high-speed 40m long, 10m wide Filo Jet vessel - sails under the flag of Turkey, according to Marine Traffic.
Filo Denizcilik, the company which operates the capsized passenger boat, said it was "deeply saddened by the tragic accident".
The TRNC controls the northern third of the island of Cyprus, which has been divided since 1974.

EU forces boarded an oil tanker suspected of belonging to Russia’s shadow fleet in the Mediterranean for a flag verification, the bloc’s foreign policy chief said Monday.
Kaja Kallas said the MV SUN was boarded Sunday by forces from the EU’s Mediterranean naval mission, Operation IRINI, over suspicions that it was sailing under a false flag in violation of international maritime law.
“Illegal oil sales from shadow fleet ships are a critical lifeline for Russia’s war in Ukraine, and we’ll continue to cut them off,” Kallas said on the US social media company X.
She added that the MV SUN was the sixth suspected shadow fleet vessel boarded by EU operations in recent months.
Measures targeting Russia’s shadow fleet will be discussed when EU defense ministers meet in Ireland on Tuesday, according to Kallas.

Families of those missing after Nepal floods struggle to cling to hope
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
11:39:10 UTC
20:39:10 KST

Nepal flood rescue recovery efforts keep hope alive for desperate families as 4,200 people remain missing
Kathmandu, Nepal — Five days after a rocky mountainside and the glacier it supported collapsed near Nepal's border with Tibet, unleashing torrents of flash floodwater, mud and debris on the valleys below that swept away everything in their path, rescuers were still searching Monday for reasons to hope.
Over the weekend, a 6-year-old girl was miraculously pulled from the mud-covered rubble, fueling hope that more of the 4,200 people still listed as missing in the wake of the disaster could be found alive.
Nepal's national disaster agency said Monday that at least 903 people had been killed, and the fear is that the toll will spiral as recovery efforts continue along the scars carved into the landscape by the raging floods.
But the danger hasn't passed. The sacred Trishuli River was surging again Monday, this time from heavy monsoon rains that have spurred search and rescue teams to try and move even faster to find anyone still alive in the ruins.
Samarth Srivastav was among the thousands of people desperately hoping a loved one might still emerge from the layers of thick mud and rubble in the Himalayan valleys.
"We're just trying to hope for good news now," Samarth told CBS News from Atlanta.
His father Vivek was on the Nepal-Tibet border when the disaster struck last week.
Samarth said his father joked with him on their last phone call about how steep the river valley walls around him were, saying, "You know, if I fall down there, like, I'll get swept away."
Just hours after the call, a tsunami of glacial ice, water and mud swept away Tibet's immigration checkpoint on the border, and Vivek hasn't been heard from since.
"Initially after hearing about it, you know, it was kind of like, okay, you know, maybe by the end of the day, you know? Might hear something back. And then the next day came and we didn't hear anything all day. And then more and more," he said. "As the number of missing people on record started to increase and, like, the severity of the situation actually started to hit, you know — we're seeing all these videos pop up on social media of people recording the disaster and everything that actually happened — I think that's when we actually started to get worried and realize that something might actually be wrong. This is actually a really bad situation."
Since then, Samarth said it has been nothing but "increasing anxiety" for his family.
"We still have the hope that he's probably okay — he's able to come back, he's probably doing fine out there," he said. "But, it's the fact we don't know anything yet, is just so scary to us."
The torrents of floodwater and everything they picked up and carried with them pushed as far as 150 miles away, into neighboring India.
At Nepal's biggest hospital, in the capital Kathmandu, an outside wall has been all but covered in posters bearing the photos of bodies recovered from the calamity. Another wall, on a smaller street nearby, was starting to fill up Monday.
They are walls of the unknown dead — photos of some of the people still likely listed as missing.
Many of the images are deeply disturbing, but desperate family members have no choice but to step up to pore over the grim images, pleading for any information about missing loved ones.
In Georgia, Samarth said he was trying to keep calm, despite a lack of any information from officials in Nepal, or at home in the U.S.
"Honestly, I haven't really heard as much from the U.S. government," he said. "There's not really much else we can do except just, like, sit and pray."
Other American families with loved ones missing told CBS News over the weekend that they want more help from U.S. authorities, as well as the Chinese and Nepalese governments.
One Virginia family told CBS News on Monday they had experienced a rollercoaster of emotions as conflicting information about survivors comes out, and while some members had lost hope that a husband and wife last thought to have been in Tibet could still be found alive, others were determined to wait for confirmation.
So far, Chinese authorities have not confirmed whether any foreign tourists survived the disaster in Tibet.

No strings attached: Air Guitar World Championships return for 30th edition in Finland
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31
11:37:15 UTC
20:37:15 KST

Finnish performer Aapo “The Angus” Rautio has won the Air Guitar World Championships for a second consecutive year, taking the title in front of a home crowd in western Finland.
Make air, not war. The purpose of the Air Guitar World Championships is to promote world peace say the organisers of the annual celebration.
Now in its 30th year, the people behind the competition claim conflicts would end, climate change would stop, along with all bad things if everyone came together to play.
We're unlikely to ever find out but in the meantime, more than 50 contestants from 13 countries gathered over several days in Oulu, Finland's newly crowned European Capital of Culture to perform.
The rules are simple; over 60 seconds each person has to pretend they're playing a real guitar, with a jury of performing arts professionals judging their efforts.
Local favourite and defending champion Aapo "The Angus" Rautio secured his second successive title with a score of 34.8.
The competition formed part of the larger Delta Life summer carnival and the wider Oulu August Festival celebrations.
Japan's Nanami “Seven Seas” Nagura finished second, while Saladin “Six String Sal” Thomas took third place.
The championships were first held in 1996 and have since grown enormously, spreading an unmeasurable amount of good-natured fun and laughter with the event livestreamed to thousands more beyond Finland.
However, despite, the enthusiasm and energy of the competitors, there's little to no sign yet of world peace coming close to being declared.
We remain hopeful, with fingers at the ready.

Modi talks trade with Iranian president on SCO summit sidelines
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-31

20:35:15 KST

Modi talks trade with Iranian president on SCO summit sidelines
India wants to “expand and diversify” its trade relations with Iran, Prime Minister Narendra Modi Prime told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday, while also calling for freedom of navigation and the protection of seafarers amid the Middle East conflict.
”Reiterated our commitment to strengthening India’s long-standing friendship with Iran across diverse sectors,” Modi posted on X after meeting Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Kyrgyzstan’s capital, Bishkek, on Monday. “We want to expand and diversify our trade basket in the times to come.”
It was the first in-person meeting between the two leaders since the Middle East conflict, triggered by US-Israeli attacks on Iran, began in February. The Indian prime minister’s statement comes amid a campaign launched by the US Treasury Department to isolate Iran economically, building on Washington’s Operation Economic Outcast, a broad effort to sever Iran’s financial links around the world. The Treasury has said it will give countries timelines to shut down Iran-related activity, and entities that fail to comply face potential secondary-sanctions.
India is among Iran’s five largest trading partners, but bilateral trade has declined more than 90% from about $17 billion in 2018-19 to about $1.6 billion in the financial year ending March 2026. Indian exports to Iran are now limited mostly to goods exempted on humanitarian grounds.
Met President Masoud Pezeshkian in Bishkek. Reiterated our commitment to strengthening India’s long standing friendship with Iran across diverse sectors. We want to expand and diversify our trade basket in the times to come. 
We had a discussion on the prevailing situation in… pic.twitter.com/qagQy5o108
Iran and the US traded attacks overnight Monday, the first time in over a month. Modi said he and the Iranian president discussed the prevailing situation in the Middle East, and that “India will continue to support all efforts aimed at ensuring lasting peace.”
The prime minister “expressed concern at the escalation of tensions” and “reiterated India’s consistent position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy,” the Indian Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
Modi also called for safeguarding the freedom of navigation and commerce and emphasized that civilians and civilian infrastructure, including commercial shipping and seafarers, must not be harmed under any circumstances. Ten Indian seafarers have died in attacks on commercial shipping around the Strait of Hormuz since the start of hostilities in February.
Modi also said he looked forward to welcoming Pezeshkian to India for the BRICS Summit in New Delhi in September. Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi was also present during the meeting.

"This is the largest defence export deal in the history of Israel-Greece relations and one of the largest in the history of the State of Israel," it added.
The deal was signed by the Israeli defence ministry's director general, Major General Amir Baram and his Greek counterpart, Ioannis Bouras, in Tel Aviv.
A Greek defence ministry source had told the AFP news agency in late July about an upcoming purchase of Israeli-made anti-missile, anti-aircraft and anti-drone systems, part of a broader defence investment for the Achilles Shield of €4.2 billion.
In a statement, the Greek Defence Ministry said the multi-billion euro purchase was part of "the greatest reform of its armed forces in its history."
Greek Defence Minister Nikos Dendias was quoted in the statement as saying that recent technological developments "have long rendered existing defence doctrines completely obsolete."
"Greece is the first country in the European Union to adopt" a multi-layered air defence system such as the Israeli one, he added.
According to the Israeli Defence Ministry, the export deal includes the David's Sling, Barak MX and SPYDER interception systems, air surveillance radars and "a new national command and control system".
All the equipment is manufactured by Israeli defence contractors Rafael and Israel Aerospace Industries and its subsidiary ELTA Systems.
A supplementary €26 million deal was also signed to provide Greece with Rafael's defence systems against drones, the ministry said.
"Israel and Greece share common strategic interests and face shared regional challenges," said Defence Minister Israel Katz, quoted in the statement.
"At a time when actors with hegemonic ambitions are seeking to expand their influence and undermine stability in the region, Israel and Greece will continue to deepen their defence and strategic cooperation," he said, in a likely reference to Turkey.
Greece is now one of only four European NATO members to spend at least 3% of GDP on its military, amid decades of tensions with neighbouring Turkey.
Israel has also increasingly locked horns with Turkey, having struck a disused military base in northwest Syria, claiming it wanted to avert Turkish troops deploying to the facility.
In 2023, Israel signed a deal with Germany to provide the Arrow 3 anti-ballistic missile defence system, which was expanded in December for a total value of $6.5 billion (€5.6 billion), the country's largest-ever military export contract.
