US testing Harpoon missiles Taiwan purchased
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:36 UTC
01:43:36 KST

The US Navy and Boeing Co have conducted a series of tests for land-based Harpoon anti-ship missile system being supplied to Taiwan and released footage showing the system striking a target vessel at sea.
The weapons system and support equipment tested were reportedly tailored for Taiwan, while the first launch vehicles and other components have already begun arriving in Taiwan, with the full delivery of 100 systems scheduled to be completed by the end of 2028.
Pentagon officials have previously told a US congressional hearing that Taiwan has “top priority worldwide” in the delivery of Harpoon missile systems, with production lines operating at full capacity to address threats in the Taiwan Strait.
Photo: Screen grab from US Navy’s Web site
The navy has budgeted more than NT$90.2 billion (US$2.85 billion) for the procurement of the systems, as part of a program running from 2021 to 2030 to establish a dense network of land-based anti-ship missile defenses.
Taiwan has purchased 100 land-based Harpoon Coastal Defense Systems from the US, which included 400 missiles, four training missiles, 100 missile launch vehicles and 25 radar vehicles. Several launch vehicles, command-and-control vehicles and radar vehicles have arrived in Taiwan, and the navy’s Littoral Combat Command is conducting equipment acceptance and simulated strike training.
The procurement is scheduled to be completed by the end of 2028.
The missiles being acquired by Taiwan are the latest upgraded RGM-84L-4 Harpoon Block II (U) land-based anti-ship missiles. They are equipped with enhanced resistance to electronic countermeasures, which would allow them to identify and engage enemy vessels in heavy-jamming environments, as well as GPS guidance and active radar guidance systems.
The missiles can be used against amphibious landing forces and carrier strike groups, while also possessing a land-attack capability against military installations along the coast. Their range exceeds the about 100km range of earlier ship-launched versions, significantly expanding the area they can cover across the Taiwan Strait.
A key feature of the latest tests was the use of Oshkosh-made Heavy Expanded Mobility Tactical Trucks (HEMTTs), which are among the US military’s newest heavy-duty tactical vehicles, military news Web site Naval News reported.
Unlike the older trailer-mounted launchers supplied by Boeing to other countries, Taiwan is receiving a highly mobile configuration in which the launch system and vehicle are integrated.
Each eight-wheel-drive HEMTT launch vehicle is equipped with an armored cab and carries four Harpoon missile canisters. The vehicles are designed for rapid movement and concealed deployment over unpaved terrain, providing greater battlefield mobility and survivability than conventional commercial truck-based trailers.
Taiwan Association for Security and Development chairman Chi Tung-yun (紀東昀) said his organization obtained four photographs of the land-based Harpoon system in southern Taiwan last year.
The equipment shown in the photographs almost completely matches footage released by the US military, Chi said.
The photographs show Harpoon missile launch vehicles that differ from those used by Denmark and South Korea, but they use the same Oshkosh HEMTT 8x8 heavy tactical truck chassis as Patriot missile systems, while carrying a new type of missile, he said.
The photographs’ backgrounds were altered using artificial intelligence to obscure identifying details, while text on the transport trailers was removed, he said.
Researchers at the Institute for National Defense and Security Research have previously said that once the US-made Harpoon systems are fully deployed, they would be integrated with Taiwan-made Hsiung Feng II (Brave Wind II, 雄風二型) and Hsiung Feng III anti-ship missiles.
The systems are expected to be linked to the navy’s Littoral Combat Command, creating a layered coastal defense network designed to deter and disrupt an amphibious assault.
The deployment is part of Taiwan’s broader effort to develop a highly mobile, distributed anti-ship capability aimed at countering Chinese military operations across the Taiwan Strait.
China deployed a record number of coast guard, scientific research and other ships near Taiwan’s waters last month, the Coast Guard Administration (CGA) said, as Beijing dials up pressure on Taipei. The coast guard warned of an increasingly severe situation, as analysts say the increased activity is part of China’s bid to map the region for submarine warfare. The number of Chinese ships detected around Taiwan proper soared to a record 244 last month — an average of nearly eight every day, official data showed. That compares with 55 ships detected in June and 30 in May, and 58 in July last year. In

NT$1bn proposed for Eswatini project
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:36 UTC
01:43:36 KST

The government has proposed spending NT$1 billion (US$31.6 million) to build an innovative industrial park in Eswatini, aiming to support industrial upgrading and economic transformation in Taiwan’s sole African ally while helping Taiwanese businesses expand their global presence.
According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ budget proposal for the next fiscal year sent to lawmakers last week for review, the ministry has proposed total expenditure of NT$43.41 billion, an increase of more than NT$3.8 billion from its budget for this fiscal year.
Among the proposed expenditure, the ministry has earmarked NT$1 billion to fund the Taiwan Industrial Innovation Park (TIIP) project in Eswatini.
Photo courtesy of the Presidential Office
The TIIP project is expected to attract more Taiwanese businesses to invest in Eswatini and help them “further expand their presence in the African market,” the ministry’s budget proposal said.
“The project will also help create local jobs, foster industrial clustering and hub development, and thereby achieve the goals of bolstering the allied nation’s prosperity and, in turn, consolidating diplomatic ties,” the proposal said.
The budget proposal is pending lawmaker approval.
President William Lai (賴清德) and Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍) have visited the planned site for the first phase of the TIIP project, which is located in Phocweni, Eswatini. It covers about 158 hectares adjacent to the Royal Science and Technology Park.
During his state visit to Eswatini in May, Lai inspected the planned TIIP site and called Eswatini a steadfast ally of Taiwan in Africa and an important gateway for Taiwanese enterprises seeking to enter the African market.
“We look forward to fostering deeper economic and trade cooperation with Eswatini through the TIIP. Doing so will attract even more Taiwanese enterprises to invest in Eswatini and cultivate local talent. In turn, this will create local jobs, enable more local businesses to join global supply chains, and enhance Eswatini’s national economic resilience,” Lai said.
About 60 Taiwanese companies have visited Eswatini to explore investment opportunities since the launch of the TIIP project in April, the ministry said.
Among them, 10 Taiwanese companies in key sectors such as textiles, packaging, pharmaceuticals and solar power have signed letters of intent indicating plans to move into the TIIP in the future.

Taipei Zoo celebrates giant panda’s 22nd birthday
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:35 UTC
01:43:35 KST

The Taipei Zoo yesterday celebrated giant panda Yuan Yuan’s (圓圓) 22nd birthday with a feast featuring a “fruit and vegetable train” loaded with specially prepared treats.
The zoo live-streamed the event on Facebook, showing the panda reaching for sweet sugar cane first among the offerings.
Visitors were cheering “Yuan Yuan, I love you,” the zoo said.
Photo: Chiang Ying-ying, AP
Keepers designed a birthday meal featuring pineapple, carrots, grapes, kiwifruit, sugar cane, honeydew melon, pumpkin and cucumber. The treats were arranged alongside golden bamboo and arrow bamboo stalks.
Bamboo makes up the main part of a giant panda’s diet, the zoo said, adding that the birthday meal was designed not only as a nutritious seasonal snack, but an exercise to stimulate Yuan Yuan’s senses and encourage exploration as she searches for food she likes.
Such enrichment activities help improve her quality of life through greater dietary variety and behavioral stimulation, the zoo added.
Now in her senior years, Yuan Yuan receives care that goes beyond simply providing food and rest, it said.
Keepers regularly monitor her weight, appetite, activity levels and behavior, while adjusting medical care, diet and environmental enrichment based on changes in her physical and behavioral condition, it said.
Special attention is given to dental care for elderly pandas, the zoo said.
While hard bamboo stalks provide necessary fiber, they can also wear down teeth, so keepers carefully control the amount of stalks Yuan Yuan receives and supplement her diet with a variety of bamboo leaves, it added.
Adjusting food portions and bamboo varieties also helps maintain healthy gut microbiota, it added.
Keepers conduct giant panda training sessions and educational talks at 3pm on the third Wednesday of every month in the Giant Panda House, so that visitors can learn more about panda care, the zoo said.

Man’s story of being tracked down for taking receipt from trash sparks debate
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:35 UTC
01:43:35 KST

A man’s story about being tracked down and questioned by police after taking a discarded receipt from a trash can has sparked a heated debate on social media.
“These days, you cannot even pick up receipts from the trash,” the poster wrote on Threads last week.
He said he found the receipt in a trash can intended for discarded slips and coupons near a payment kiosk, but was surprised when he was contacted by police to give a statement after the original owner of the receipt filed a complaint alleging misappropriation.
Photo: Clare Cheng, Taipei Times
He wrote that he was found through a review of surveillance footage and a license-plate match.
Commenters in the thread were divided on the matter, with some saying that the receipt’s original owner had relinquished ownership by throwing it away.
“If you cannot even pick something out of a trash can, it is probably safer to stay well away from anything you see lying around,” another commenter wrote.
Others said that the receipt being found in the trash can did not necessarily mean the owner intended to relinquish ownership of it.
Some commenters said that they have seen store clerks tear up receipts in front of customers to prevent disputes if someone else picked them up.
Another person wrote that as receipts could be used to claim winnings in the uniform invoice lottery, the issue could be complicated if it turned out to be a winning receipt.
Lawyer Lee Hsueh-yung (李學鏞) said that whether picking up a receipt constitutes misappropriation of lost property cannot be determined solely by whether it was “picked up” or “left in a trash can.”
It generally depends on whether the person intended to take the item for themselves, whether they actually took possession of it, and whether the item was lost property or an ownerless object that had been intentionally abandoned, he said.
If the original owner intentionally discarded the receipt, it could be considered ownerless property, meaning the person who picked it up could, in principle, take ownership of the item by taking possession of it, Lee said.
However, if the receipt had been dropped accidentally or the owner had mistakenly thrown away an item that still had value, its legal status could be different, he said.
If the person who picked it up did not subsequently redeem it for a prize or otherwise make use of its value, whether they had the intent to misappropriate it would still have to be determined based on the available evidence, Lee said.

Fed chair signals rate hikes might be needed with US inflation still elevated
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:35 UTC
01:43:35 KST

US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday said inflation is still too high and suggested that the central bank might have to raise interest rates in the coming months to bring it down, a clearer signal than he has previously sent about his economic outlook.
Warsh during the Fed’s annual conference in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, acknowledged that US reports showed that inflation has cooled a bit, but “they do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.”
“We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed,” he said. “Otherwise, we have work to do.”
Photo: Bloomberg
The comments appeared to reassure Wall Street that fighting inflation remains the priority for the central bank.
Warsh did not imply that a rate hike is imminent, but appeared to dismiss perceptions that inflation is no longer a threat.
He pointed to data showing that inflation remains stubbornly above the central bank’s 2 percent target.
Warsh has said he does not want to provide what analysts call “forward guidance” about whether the Fed would hike or cut rates, or stay on hold at its policy meetings.
It limits the Fed’s flexibility by committing it to a specific policy, he said.
Yet some economists said he could say more about his views on Fed policy without tipping his hand about future actions.
Warsh reiterated his skepticism about providing such guidance or even outlining his broad approach to interest rate policy, but did suggest that interest rates are not restricting economic activity, pointing to robust business investment in artificial intelligence equipment and infrastructure, and strong consumer spending.
As a rule of thumb, interest rates often need to be high enough to limit borrowing and spending to cool inflation.
The Fed next meets on Sept. 15 to 16.
Wall Street investors see the chances of a rate hike at the next meeting as basically a coin flip, futures pricing tracked by CME FedWatch showed, up from about one-third before Warsh spoke.
Warsh said that inflation data “are more concerning” than trends in the job market, where the unemployment rate is low, adding that inflation is unlikely to move back to the target on its own.
In the past year, more than half of goods and services tracked by the government have seen price increases of 3 percent or higher, he said.
While that is down from the COVID-19 pandemic peak, it is “well above” the roughly one-third that saw such increases in the two decades before the pandemic, he added.
Inflation cooled in June and last month after spiking in May from soaring gas prices, but remains above the central bank’s target.
According to the Fed’s preferred measure, it was 3.7 percent last month.
Warsh also sought to clear up some areas of confusion that arose after his remarks at the July 29 news conference, when he made vague remarks about what metric the Fed would use to track inflation and whether short-term interest rates were the Fed’s main tool to combat higher prices.
Short-term interest rates are the Fed’s “predominant tool,” he said, adding that the central bank is using the same gauge it has long followed to measure inflation.

Iceland votes ‘No’ to resuming EU membership talks
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:33 UTC
01:43:33 KST

Iceland voted ‘No’ to resuming membership negotiations with the EU, final referendum results showed yesterday, dealing a blow to Brussels which had been keen to welcome an affluent member.
In a vote held on Saturday, 52.8 percent of Icelanders rejected the resumption of EU entry talks suspended 13 years ago, while 47.2 percent voted ‘Yes,’ according to the official tally published by RUV, the public broadcaster.
The result would be a disappointment to Brussels, which had appeared willing to compromise on thorny issues to facilitate Iceland’s accession.
Photo: AP
The result would also likely bury the EU question in Iceland until at least 2028.
Far-right leaders in Britain and France hailed the result.
“At a time when some are pushing for greater federalism and the transfer of sovereignty to the European Commission, this vote reminds us that another Europe is possible, a Europe of free, sovereign nations cooperating voluntarily on matters of common interest,” former French far-right leader Marine Le Pen wrote on X.
“Congratulations to Iceland on voting to keep their independence,” Reform UK leader Nigel Farage wrote on the same platform.
The country of fewer than 400,000 people applied to join the EU in the wake of a 2009 financial crisis that devastated its economy. Membership talks were then suspended in 2013 when a eurosceptic government came to power.
Amid growing international tensions, the Icelandic government headed by Social Democratic Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir wanted to sound out Icelanders on deepening their ties to the EU.
The island is already closely linked to the EU as a member of the European Economic Area and the free-movement Schengen zone, ties which would remain unchanged.
The referendum result is non-binding, but the government has vowed to respect it.
Debates ahead of the vote had mainly revolved around domestic and economic issues, although the war in Ukraine and US President Donald Trump’s ambitions for neighboring Greenland — which he has mixed up with Iceland on several occasions — also featured.
The campaign had “lifted discussions about the EU, about Iceland’s place in the world, about our general geopolitical situation and status, to a higher level,” Frostadottir said on Saturday after she cast her ballot.
She was openly in favor of a ‘Yes,’ but “we will be fine also if it’s a ‘No,’” she said.
Frostadottir had vowed that in the event of ‘No,’ the EU membership issue would not be put back on the political agenda during her mandate, which ends in 2028.
Political analysts said it was unlikely the government would resign in the event of a ‘No’ victory, but it could emerge weakened by the rejection.
The campaign divided Iceland down the middle. Voter turnout was 82.5 percent, the highest participation in any Icelandic vote since April 2009 parliamentary elections during its crippling financial crisis, according to RUV.
“I’m maybe in a kind of denial that this has happened. It’s hard to grasp that it’s a ‘No,’” 37-year-old artist Elisabet Anna Kristjansdottir said. “It’s quite sad that the Icelandic people don’t even want to see the possibilities of joining the EU.”

At least 8 dead, 17 missing after ferry capsizes off Northern Cyprus
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30

01:43:28 KST

At least 8 dead, 17 missing after ferry capsizes off Northern Cyprus
Captain and crew arrested after survivors report explosion on bow before vessel sank into deep waters
A passenger ferry capsized and sank off Northern Cyprus Sunday, killing at least eight people and leaving more than a dozen missing, officials and media reports said, as police took the captain and seven crew members into custody.
Several rescued passengers told local media a blast had gone off at the bow of the ferry before it rolled over, and said the boat had an insufficient supply of life-vests.
The vessel capsized 6.5km (4 miles) off the coast of Cyprus, shortly after leaving a Northern Cyprus port bound for Turkey’s mainland.
Images broadcast by Turkish television showed the upside-down ferry in the water, with people wearing life vests atop its orange hull.
“Some people had to jump without lifebuoys or life jackets,” one young man, Efe Multici, told CNN Turk. “It was literally a fight for survival.”
The ferry had been carrying a total of 267 people, according to authorities, of which 161 were rescued and taken to hospital and 76 have returned home.

North Korea’s defense minister has been dismissed as part of a reshuffle of the country’s military leadership, state media reported yesterday.
The “structural reorganization plans” were decided during a meeting on Saturday led by North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said.
No Kwang-chol was not only dismissed as defense minister, but also demoted in the ruling party leadership to “first vice-director of the Munitions Industry Department,” KCNA said.
Photo: the Korean Central News Agency via Reuters
Kim Song-gi, director of the General Political Bureau of the Korean People’s Army, was named as the new defense minister.
Another senior official, defense adviser Pak Jong-chon, was given the position of vice-chairman of the North Korean Central Military Commission and named to the ruling party’s Political Bureau.
Several other promotions were also announced.
In a separate report, KCNA said Kim had on Saturday lauded scientists, researchers and officials at a ceremony for their advances in defense technology, giving them top national honors.
The honorees greatly contributed to “resolving scientific and technological problems of epochal significance in developing new combat weapon systems,” KCNA said, without specifying the type of system.
A photo released by KCNA shows Kim pinning a medal on a recipient. The nuclear-armed state’s weapons research center “has recently developed exclusive technologies, to be regarded as an event in strengthening the capability for fighting a war,” it added without giving details.
With such technologies, it has shown “the course of unique development of the country’s military and technological capabilities,” it said.
In late June, Kim oversaw tests of a new extended-range multiple rocket launcher and artillery.
The leadership shuffle comes shortly after joint annual drills between South Korea and the US wrapped up.
The drills, which are regularly denounced by Pyongyang as preparations for an invasion, were closely watched this year after US President Donald Trump ordered them to be cut short.

Taiwan-US astronaut throws 1st pitch
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:25 UTC
01:43:25 KST

Taiwan-born astronaut Kjell Lindgren threw the ceremonial first pitch at the Washington Nationals’ Taiwan Heritage Day at Nationals Park on Saturday before the game against the Miami Marlins.
Speaking before the Nationals’ second Taiwanese Heritage Day, Lindgren said throwing the first pitch was “right up there in terms of anxiety-provoking” with some of his past accomplishments, including two rocket launches, two atmospheric reentries and two spacewalks.
“But I’m really excited to be a part of this celebration of Taiwan heritage,” he said, adding that it was “an opportunity to really celebrate the relationship, the partnership, the history between the United States and Taiwan.”
Photo: CNA
Lindgren said he was “very excited” about future opportunities for Taiwan and the US to partner as they move forward with spacefaring efforts to explore the moon and beyond.
The astronaut was chosen for his accomplishments and his ties to the US and Taiwan through his multicultural heritage, organizer Millennial Global Youth (MGY) Foundation said earlier this month.
Lindgren, whose Chinese name is Lin Chi-erh (林琪兒), was born in Taipei to a Taiwanese mother and an American father stationed in Taipei with the US Air Force.
Saturday’s event featured several booths around Nationals Park promoting Taiwanese culture, as well as a performance of the US national anthem by Taiwanese American singer-songwriter Vienna Teng (史逸欣) and a performance by Formosan Groove, a musical fusion project incorporating Taiwanese and American elements.
Participants could enter a raffle to win a round-trip flight between Washington and Taiwan from EVA Air, according to the MGY Foundation.
About 700 tickets were sold for the event, organizers said.
Saturday was the third time Lindgren has thrown a ceremonial first pitch at a Taiwan-related professional baseball event.
In April, he threw the first pitch at a game between the Rakuten Monkeys and Wei Chuan Dragons at Rakuten Taoyuan Baseball Stadium in Taiwan. Last month, he joined CPBL Commissioner Tsai Chi-chang to throw the first pitch at the New York Mets’ Taiwan Heritage Day.
The MGY Foundation is a group composed mainly of second-generation Taiwanese-Americans that promotes Taiwanese culture, multicultural diversity and community ties.

TIPC establishes command center at Kaohsiung Port
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:25 UTC
01:43:25 KST

Taiwan International Ports Corp (TIPC) has established an operations command center at the Kaohsiung Port Cruise Terminal to monitor all commercial ports under its jurisdiction.
The terminal — which opened in 2023 and features a silver-white hull with a towering funnel-like structure — was built to transform Kaohsiung into a world-class international cruise travel hub. It has become a landmark of Kaohsiung’s Asia New Bay Area.
The terminal houses a state-of-the-art operations command center, which was unveiled during a visit last week.
Photo courtesy of a reader
TIPC operates international commercial ports in Keelung, Taipei, Taichung, Kaohsiung, Hualien County, Tainan’s Anping (安平) and Yilan County’s Suao Township (蘇澳), the company said.
It also oversees the operations of two domestic commercial ports: one in Chiayi County’s Budai Township (布袋) and another in Penghu County’s Magong Port.
The command center is equipped with a system that consolidates critical real-time information from all commercial ports, enhancing the company’s ability to monitor, report and respond to natural disasters and other emergencies, TIPC said.
Photo: Wu Liang-yi, Taipei Times
The terminal is powered by an intelligent microgrid system, combining a 12.7 kilowatt-peak solar power generation system with a 1 megawatt / 2 megawatt-hour energy storage system, it said.
In addition to managing peak electricity demand and enhancing energy dispatch flexibility, the power grid enables energy self-management at the port, reducing carbon dioxide emissions by an estimated 250 tonnes per year, it said.
The server room follows international energy-efficiency standards, the company said.
Through precise temperature and humidity controls and smart cooling design, it has optimized power usage effectiveness to below 1.52, TIPC said, adding that this is expected to significantly reduce annual energy consumption and cut carbon emissions by about 12 tonnes.
The operator also unveiled plans to revamp the area around the Port of Kaohsiung.
“We want to transform the old port zone into a waterfront leisure zone that serves as a flexible interface between the city and the sea, breaks down barriers between the port and the city, and uses light rail to connect the two,” TIPC deputy general manager Cheng Chih-wen (鄭智文) said. “We are learning from the zone-based management model set by Japan’s Port of Yokohama, which uses an elevated walkway to block noises produced by port logistic services and paved the water-access promenade.”
The company learned from South Korea’s Port of Busan that a port-driven economy could be developed by combining the port’s international business convention center with culture and leisure, he said.
“We aim to create a value-added industry chain by combining the Port of Kaohsiung’s international convention center, Warehouse No. 2 and the Pier-2 Art Center,” Cheng added.
The company plans to recruit a contractor to open a coffee house at the top of the terminal, where the shop would have a panoramic view of the port, he said.

‘Lake Ontario’ sign put as Canadians mock Trump
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:23 UTC
01:43:23 KST

Ontario Premier Doug Ford on Saturday answered US President Donald Trump’s “Lake America” decree with a billboard-sized message on the Canadian shoreline — “Lake Ontario. Now and Always” — as Canadian leaders met Trump’s move with ridicule rather than outrage.
Wearing a Canada national soccer team jersey, Ford unveiled the sign near Grimsby and posed for photographs. The message is repeated in French.
The display followed Trump’s executive order directing US federal agencies to call Lake Ontario “Lake America.” After months of tariffs, threats to make Canada the 51st US state and personal attacks on its leaders, the reaction in Canada has mixed defiance with mockery.
Photo: Reuters
Trump was trying to rename the lake, because Ontario and Canada were “standing up for ourselves,” Ford said, adding that the name would outlast the US president.
“Long after President Trump is gone, it will still be called Lake Ontario,” Ford said in a video posted on social media.
Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew compared Trump to an aging rock band trying to revive an old hit.
“You know when a rock band is really over the hill, and you see them like in a casino playing some song from like 50 years ago. I think that’s the part of Donald Trump’s presidency we’re at now. Like he thought they had a real hit, a real golden oldie, with the Gulf of Mexico,” Kinew said, referring to Trump’s executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America. “And he’s trying to bring back that, and he’s trying to play the hits for his base, but I think everybody here thinks it’s a little sad, and it’s not his best work.”
The mockery was not limited to politicians. Canadian historian Robert Bothwell was even more scathing.
“The greatest country on earth takes this moron seriously?” Bothwell asked.
However, he said the dispute was more serious than the jokes, adding that Trump’s broader aim was “to subordinate Canada and at best make it a colony, at worst absorb it into the United States.”
Nelson Wiseman, professor emeritus at the University of Toronto, said Trump “would like Canada to act like a vassal state, but it refuses to do so. That irritates him.”
The dispute comes as relations between the longtime allies worsen over trade. Negotiations collapsed last week, both governments accused the other of making late demands, and Canada announced retaliatory tariffs set to take effect next month.
Trump’s order also came amid an escalating war of words with Ford. In an interview earlier this week, Ford said former US president Ronald Reagan would be “throwing up” over Trump’s tariff policies and “disgusted with President Trump.”
Trump fired back by dismissing Ford’s comments as “bluster,” calling him Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s “flunky” and mocking him as the “less charismatic, intelligent and overall unimpressive brother” of the late Toronto mayor Rob Ford.
Trump on Saturday continued promoting the new name, reposting a meme showing Canada geese with Trump-like blond hair firing rifles as they “protected” “Lake America.”
Trump has repeatedly used maps to make political points. A “Gulf of America” map was displayed for a time beside the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office, and Trump has posted images depicting Canada as part of the US or as the 51st state.
The name Lake Ontario comes from the Huron indigenous people’s word “oniatari:io,” which means “lake of shining waters.” The Canadian province of Ontario, founded in 1867, took its name from the lake.
Wendat Nation Grand Chief Pierre Picard, whose people historically lived from the St Lawrence Valley to the Great Lakes and whose language gave Lake Ontario its name, called Trump’s move an attempt to erase indigenous history.
“I want to tell him that it is unacceptable for us, as a nation, to have a president who can eradicate our history, our culture and our identity,” Picard said.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the move, saying that the lake’s indigenous roots and the name predate both Canadian Confederation and the US Declaration of Independence. Trump cannot require Canada to adopt the new name.

Military updates arsenal with automated systems
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:21 UTC
01:43:21 KST

A newly relocated military arsenal in Kaohsiung has significantly improved its safety management and production capacity through the use of automated systems, as part of the military’s ongoing efforts to bolster its indigenous defense capabilities, the arsenal’s chief said yesterday.
Major General Huang Chiao-chan (黃教展), head of the 205th Arsenal of the Ministry of National Defense’s Armaments Bureau, spoke during a media tour of the arsenal, the first of its kind since the arsenal was relocated from its former site in Kaohsiung’s Cianjhen District (前鎮) to the current location in Dashu District (大樹).
Founded in 1945, the Armaments Bureau’s 205th Arsenal has been responsible for producing infantry arms of calibers below 40mm for Taiwan’s armed forces.
Photo: Aaron Tu, Taipei Times
Under Kaohsiung’s “Asia New Bay Area” project, which aims to transform the city’s old industrial areas into new industrial, exhibition and cultural sites, the arsenal completed its relocation to two bases in Dashu District by the end of last year.
Asked about the relocation, Huang said the new facilities underwent a comprehensive upgrade, including the integration of smart technologies and automated management systems.
These improvements mitigate security risks that were associated with the old facilities, and also provide a better working environment and living quarters for military personnel, he said.
Huang said the 205th Arsenal is primarily responsible for the research, development and production of small arms of 40mm caliber or smaller, as well as ammunition, explosives and combat gear.
Its products include the T75K3 9mm semi-automatic service pistol, T75 5.56mm light machine gun, T74 7.62mm medium machine gun, T90 .50 BMG heavy machine gun, and T75 20mm autocannon.
One of the arsenal’s top priorities is the T112 assault rifle.
The latest generation of the domestically developed assault rifle was designed and developed by the bureau starting in 2020 and passed acceptance trials in late 2023.
The army purchased an initial batch of 25,000 T112 rifles last year. The ministry has allocated NT$8.1 billion (US$257.5 million) to purchase a total of 86,114 T112 rifles from last year to 2029, with all to be produced by the 205th Arsenal.
The latest-generation rifles are to be used by Taiwan’s combat units, replacing the older T91 rifles, the ministry said.
During the tour, reporters were also shown the T112 manufacturing process.
According to Colonel Lin Wei (林威), an official at the 205th Arsenal in charge of rifle production, the arsenal is capable of manufacturing all six key components of the rifle itself: the barrel, bolt carrier group, upper and lower receivers, firing pin and bolt release.
Other components are manufactured by local suppliers, he said.
The new factory’s production line is equipped with robotic arms and an automated management system to reduce manpower requirements and improve quality, Lin said.
The ministry’s Armaments Bureau is one of the two major weapons manufacturers for the armed forces.
In addition to the 205th Arsenal in Kaohsiung, the bureau operates three other arsenals in Taiwan: the 202nd Arsenal in Taipei’s Nangang District (南港), which produces weapons systems with calibers larger than 40mm; the 209th Arsenal in Nantou County, which manufactures armored vehicles; and the 401st Arsenal, which produces optoelectronic equipment and surveying systems.
The other major weapons manufacturer for the armed forces is the National Chungshan Institute of Science and Technology, which is responsible for producing missile systems.

Alleged vote-buying in Hualien to be investigated
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:19 UTC
01:43:19 KST

The Hualien District Prosecutors’ Office yesterday launched an investigation following allegations by a former foreign correspondent in Taiwan of widespread vote-buying in Hualien County.
In an interview with Formosa TV (FTV, 民視) aired on Saturday, former Financial Times Taiwan correspondent Kathrin Hille spoke about Taiwan’s democracy and said that she now lives in rural Hualien, where “all the votes are bought.”
Neighbors would talk about who had come by and leave cash on the table showing “how much each vote was worth that year,” Hille said.
Photo: Wang Chin-yi, Taipei Times
The practice needs to be addressed, considering Taiwan has been a democracy for many years, she said.
In response to media queries for comment on Hille’s remarks, Hualien Chief Prosecutor Liao Jung-kuan (廖榮寬) yesterday said that prosecutors have assigned it for investigation.
Authorities are investigating vote-buying cases, he said, calling on the public to help safeguard fair and impartial elections and warned candidates not to break the law.
Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Hualien County Councilor Hu Jen-shun (胡仁順) yesterday said Hualien’s corrupt election environment is nothing new, and for years, prosecutors and investigators have pledged to conduct aggressive crackdowns, but to no avail.
Hopefully they prosecute someone this time, and “don’t start taking the issue seriously just because a foreign national [Hille] brought it up,” he said.
The DPP has very limited resources in the county, so most of its candidates continue to seek voters’ support through low-cost, open and transparent methods during elections, such as door-to-door campaigning and holding policy presentation events, while supporting judicial authorities’ “anti-bribery and encouraging reporting” campaigns, he added.
The Chinese Nationalist Party’s (KMT) Hualien County commissioner candidate Candy Yu (游淑貞) yesterday said Hille painted all elected representatives with a broad brush and dismissed their efforts.
Yu said Hille should provide concrete evidence, adding that otherwise she does not rule out legal action against her, as her remark constitutes an attack on the character of hardworking representatives, and amounts to slander and defamation.
Independent Hualian County commissioner candidates Chang Chun (張峻) and Wei Chia-hsien (魏嘉賢), former KMT members, also urged Hille to provide evidence to back her claim.
Prosecutors should investigate the situation, and clear voters in Hualien of this accusation if no such activity is found, they said.
The Hualien County Government declined to comment, saying the issue is not within its jurisdiction.
The Hualien County Election Commission said its role is to administer election operations, and investigating vote-buying is beyond its scope of duties.
Meanwhile, election-related enforcement records over the years suggested the severity of vote-buying in Hualien.
In 2018, investigators uncovered cases in which as much as NT$10,000 (US$316) was allegedly paid for a single vote.
Hualien has long been one of the areas where the most rewards for reporting vote-buying have been paid. Of the NT$500 million in reporting rewards issued nationwide in 2018, about 10 percent went to cases in Hualien.
During the 2022 election, the Hualien District Prosecutors’ Office mounted a major crackdown, conducting searches at 72 locations and questioning 147 people. Prosecutors sought detention for seven suspects, all of whom were placed in custody, and seized more than NT$620,000 in suspected vote-buying funds.
Acting Prosecutor-General Hsu Hsi-hsiang (徐錫祥) in June traveled to Hualien to launch operations against vote-buying.
Vote-buying is not always a one-way transaction, investigators said, adding that some voters would offer to sell their votes, asking candidates for cash or even free meals and entertainment in return.
Some voters have come to regard vote-buying as part of the political process, and candidates do not necessarily hand out money indiscriminately, the investigators said.
Political staffers often maintain so-called “safe lists” of voters known to be willing to take cash, they said.
With neither party reporting the other and both sides protecting one another, vote-buying can be extremely difficult for authorities to uncover, they said.

BOOKMAN BILINGUAL 雙語書林： Chinglish or Natural English? 中式英語或道地英語？
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:16 UTC
01:43:16 KST

1. 我跟室友學了一點法語。
ˇ I have acquired a little knowledge of French from my roommate.
ˇ I have learned a little French from my roommate.
Photo: AdobeStock l 圖片:AdobeStock
χ I have learned a little knowledge of French from my roommate.
註︰表達「習得某種知識」，可以說 to acquire a good knowledge / some knowledge / a little knowledge。
to learn 或 to study 不可以和 knowledge 搭配。
2. 他請她喝一杯葡萄酒，她接受了。
ˇ He offered her a glass of wine, which she accepted.
χ He offered her a cup of wine, which she received.
註︰酒杯通常用 glass，不用 cup。receive 是「收到」；accept 是「接受」。從下例中可看出其涵義不同：
I received his gift yesterday, but I do not think I will accept it.。
3. 他答應替我做這件事。
ˇ He promised to do this for me.
χ He allowed to do this for me.
註︰allow 作「允許別人做某件事」解時，後面接受詞與不定詞。例如：
He allowed me to do so.
作「允許給某人某物」解時，後面接直接受詞。例如：
The teacher allowed us two weeks to write the paper.
promise 表示「動作的主體向別人允諾將做某件事」時，後面跟不定詞片語，或跟以 that 引導的受詞子句，例如：
He promised to be here at six o’clock sharp.
I promised him that I would do my best to help him.
注意下列兩句不同的意義：
He allowed me to leave the office. 他允許我離開辦公室。
（不是「他離去」，而是「我離去」。）
He promised me to leave the office. 他答應我會離開辦公室。
（是「他會離去」，不是「我離去」。）
4. 傑克從圖書館借了幾本有趣的書。
ˇ Jack borrowed some interesting books from the library.
χ Jack lent some interesting books from the library.
註︰lend「借給」、「借出」；borrow「借自」、「從…借到」。例如：
Will you lend me the book you borrowed from the library?
你從圖書館借來的書，可以借給我嗎？
5. 貓想抓那隻鳥。
ˇ The cat wanted to catch the bird.
χ The cat wanted to catch up with the bird.
註︰catch 是「捉」、「抓」；catch up (with) 是「趕上」、「追上」。
Exercises
A. 我送他一件生日禮物，他收下了。
I gave him a birthday gift, which he ____________ .
1. absorbed 2. received 3. took 4. accepted
B. 我不能借給你那本圖書館借來的書。
I cannot ________________ you the book I __________ from the library.
1. borrow; lend 2. lent; borrowed
3. borrow; lent 4. lend; borrowed
Answers: A. 4 B. 4

www.bookman.com.tw

Where is your happy place? Maybe it’s Slovenia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:16 UTC
01:43:16 KST

What if the secret to happiness was... low expectations?
Most residents of rich, Western countries have relatively high earnings, but many also feel they cannot afford a reasonable lifestyle. Americans, for example, are getting richer, but also more unhappy. Meanwhile Eastern Europeans, not generally known for their cheery disposition, are most satisfied with their comparatively lower income.
In 2018, research psychologists at Purdue and the University of Virginia compiled data from previous surveys to estimate how much income people needed to be happy. They found that, even after adjusting for purchasing power, people needed more money in richer countries. Recently, the same data was adjusted for inflation and compared with average earnings in each country.
Illustration: Yusha
Residents of Eastern European countries tend to earn at least 70 percent of what they think they need to be happy, although it also does not take so much to feel satisfied. Slovenians are the most content with their earnings: Theirs is the only country included in the study where average annual earnings (US$42,800) exceed the amount they think they need for a good life (US$36,800).
One of the few Western countries where people earn more than 70 percent of what they think they need to feel happy is Luxembourg.
The countries where people are most stretched are New Zealand, the UK and Australia, where earnings only cover about one-third of what it costs to be happy.
Of course, happiness is subjective, but what comes through in this research is that the affordability crisis is not just an American phenomenon, nor can it be solved by more government spending. In Sweden, for example, affordability is at least as big an issue as it is in the US, and like in the US, one of the main culprits is housing. Many Western countries have building restrictions and rent controls that make buying housing more expensive.
The other problem, if I can call it that, might just be rising prosperity. As countries get richer, living standards increase — maybe faster than incomes do. It is worth noting that the countries that fall the most short on this “affordable happiness” scale tend to be in Latin America, which feature low levels of desired and actual income. Again, the point is not that people in richer countries are not happier — in general, they are — but that the gains from happiness do not keep up with rising income.
The original paper also finds diminishing happiness returns to income, and then actual negative returns: People become happier as they start to earn more, but at a certain point they start becoming less happy as their income rises.
The explanation could be that once someone’s basic needs are met, they become more focused on material goals and social comparisons, the authors speculate.
Even in Denmark — one of the happiest nations in the world, according to a separate annual survey with a different methodology — average annual income covers only 66.8 percent of what people said they need to feel happy.
Capitalism might have made hundreds of millions of people rich and delivered more material wealth than the world has ever seen, but it also moved the goalposts. Market distortions that created shortages and increased prices over the past several years also caused a cost-of-living crisis that still afflicts most rich countries.
One tempting conclusion from this research is that we would all be happier with a simpler, less materialistic life. However, this would be the wrong lesson. The desire for more also accelerates progress and contributes to rising living standards. Perhaps some Kiwis would be happier if they moved to Slovenia and experienced a lower cost-of-living on their New Zealand wages, but they might not be so happy if they suddenly got paid like Slovenians.
A better lesson is that it pays to remove the distortions to commerce and economic activity that drive up prices. Nearly all the richer countries where people are not earning enough to be happy also face aging populations and big debts, and growth in a lot of Europe is stagnant. That means things could soon get even more expensive — just as a lot of people are getting poorer.
Allison Schrager is a Bloomberg Opinion columnist covering economics. A senior fellow at the Manhattan Institute, she is author of An Economist Walks Into a Brothel: And Other Unexpected Places to Understand Risk. This column reflects the personal views of the author and does not necessarily reflect the opinion of the editorial board or Bloomberg LP and its owners.

Richard D. Fisher, Jr. On Taiwan: The Coming Waves of CCP-PLA Military Deluges
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:14 UTC
01:43:14 KST

As part of its relentless pursuit of hegemony, the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and its People’s Liberation Army (PLA) are now sustaining two regional wars while threatening further arms races that shift the global balance of power in order for the CCP to advance its ultimate objective.
Russia’s and Iran’s war efforts are being materially supported by Chinese supplies of drone components and missile fuels.
So far in 2026, such Chinese support has enabled a 60 percent increase in civilian casualties in Ukraine caused by long-range Russian weapons such as missiles and drones from January to June 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, while Chinese components enabled Iran in 2026 to launch 7,400 drones and missiles against Saudi Arabia and the Gulf States.
But even short of war, the corrupting potential of Chinese power was recently illustrated by Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, who on August 16, 2026, indicated his understanding of, if not support for, China’s military “reunification” with Taiwan, telling Al Jazeera, “I see Taiwan as part of China, period… If one province decides to break away. Do we use force? I think I will, (to) protect the sanctity and unity of the nation.”
Whatever Anwar’s intentions, his statement appears to give insufficient consideration to the consequences a CCP war against Taiwan could have for Malaysia’s own security — including the possibility of a major refugee crisis and expanded Chinese military pressure in the region.
China may use a Taiwan war to justify an invasion of the Philippines’ Batanes and Palawan provinces — already coveted by CCP propagandists — potentially placing PLA military power on Malaysia’s border.
But even having suffered calumnious abuse and jailing by his China-power-corrupted predecessor Mahathir Mohamad (in October 1998, I authored a brief Heritage Foundation paper pleading Anwar’s case against Mahathir’s abuse), current Prime Minister Anwar seemingly has no problem condemning the people of Taiwan to CCP subjugation in which Taiwan’s men will be drafted to invade neighboring countries, perhaps even Malaysia.
Mahathir and Anwar are prime examples of how China has been able to exploit its galloping economic and military power to convince regional leaders to accommodate CCP goals, including support for wars against Taiwan and others, which in turn propels the CCP toward ever-grander investments and projects that shift the global balance of power in its favor.
Beyond ICBMs: One of the most audacious CCP-PLA investments underway is to make obsolete the current system of missile/nuclear deterrence based on nuclear warhead-armed intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) and submarine-launched ballistic missiles (SLBMs).
To be sure, PLA second-generation small nuclear warheads have the potential to raise the number of deployed PLA strategic nuclear warheads to 3,000 to 4,000, but this could be eclipsed by the PLA’s investment in about 23 government-linked but mainly “private” corporations seeking to become the next SpaceX — one US company that led the world with 170 space launches in 2025, almost twice China’s total.
So far in 2026, two Chinese companies have demonstrated first-stage reusable space launch vehicles (SLVs) — the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) 10-ton-to-orbit Long March-10B (July 10, 2026), and the LandSpace Corporation 8-ton-to-orbit Zhuque-3 (August 18, 2026) — which could eventually rival the 20-ton-to-orbit SpaceX Falcon-9.
Five Chinese companies are developing larger SLVs capable of placing roughly 100 tons into orbit, with reusable first stages comparable in ambition to SpaceX’s Starship.
Separately, five Chinese companies are planning megaconstellations totaling as many as 38,000 broadband satellites, compared to 42,000 planned broadband Starlink satellites from SpaceX, which have made the difference for Ukraine’s survival on the battlefield.
These Chinese megaconstellations will enable future PLA global manned and unmanned military operations, and will also provide constant targeting data for thousands of very small but highly maneuverable hypersonic glide vehicle (HGV) warheads — carried by China’s large reserve of reusable SLVs.
These will be capable of intimately targeting enemy weapons or even the domiciles of key political and military personnel, on a continuous and global scale — helping to make ICBMs obsolete.
Global Nuclear Navy: It certainly helps the CCP-PLA to shift the balance of power by having the world’s largest navy in terms of ships, as acknowledged by the US government since 2020.
But the maritime balance of power will shift further when the PLA Navy (PLAN) gains access to Chinese-subsidized and -built ports like Pakistan’s Gwadar — bracketing India and controlling access to the Persian Gulf — and Peru’s Chancay, securing access to Western Latin America and helping to secure sea lanes useful for isolating Australia and New Zealand.
That maritime balance will shift faster, however, when the PLAN is able to deploy fully nuclear-powered 35-knot aircraft carrier battle groups that perhaps could deploy from Hainan Island to New Zealand in about a week.
While the US Navy has operated nuclear-powered submarines (SSNs) since 1954 and nuclear-powered aircraft carriers (CVNs) since 1961, and only operated nuclear-powered combat cruisers from 1961 to 1999, the PLAN is now investing heavily in nuclear-powered ships.
The PLA is greatly expanding its SSN production, and could soon be hunting US Navy nuclear ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs), and may be building its first CVN.
But in September 2018, the No. 719 Research Institute of the China Shipbuilding Industry Corporation (CSIC) revealed in model form the possibility that it would develop a nuclear-powered comprehensive underway replenishment ship (AORN), a type of vessel the US Navy has never operated.
Should the PLAN also build AORNs, their ability to provide aircraft fuel, spare weapons and ship stores will only serve to compound its power projection capability, and thus the ability of the CCP to coerce and intimidate, at nuclear battle group speeds.
Solar System Control: The CCP apparently understands that achieving hegemony on Earth is for naught if it cannot control the Earth-Moon System and extend its control into the Solar System, so that the CCP becomes the primary rule-maker and arbiter for the future Space Economy.
This ambition will never be explained in a future Chinese space “White Paper,” but in August 2023, the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation, which fully reflects CCP ambitions, hosted a symposium that explained how, for the previous two years, it had been devising a 100-year plan to occupy the Solar System — or to so extend CCP control.
Controlling access to the Moon increases the PLA’s ability to control the strategic Lagrange points that enable low-power stationing of military surveillance or combat platforms.
These would include the dual-use surveillance and space combat systems for a “planetary defense system” against asteroids, as announced on state television on June 30, 2026, by Li Mingtao (李明濤) of the China National Space Administration.
Li stated, “China is currently evaluating a planetary defense system,” specifically mentioning the construction of ground and space telescopes. On that same day, state media Global Times cited oft-quoted expert Song Zhongping (宋忠平) as saying, “gravity tractors, laser ablation and continuous-thrust techniques, with the ultimate goal of nudging the asteroid away from Earth’s orbital path well in advance, preventing a potential impact.”
Expect the PLA, when it chooses, also to use “gravity tractors, laser ablation” against US or other nations’ spacecraft seeking access to the Moon, or, when surveillance and control systems are further deployed, also to control access to Mars.
The good news regarding these three realms of future CCP-PLA power projection is that the United States is also active and has the ability to help devise a broader allied response involving the larger democratic community of nations — but that will require sustained, considerable defense and science expenditures, from Washington and from its allies.
On August 20, the Trump Administration released a Presidential Memorandum on “The National Space Transportation Policy” stating, “By 2030, our space transportation ranges must grow to support more than 1,000 launches and reentries every year.”
This will require enormous private and public-sector investments in SLVs and launch facilities, but also should prompt interest among US allies that may also seek joint ventures that expand their indigenous space access capabilities — which may provide options to retaliate against the CCP-PLA’s military use of its rapidly expanding space access capabilities.
Many in Washington have cheered President Trump’s December 22, 2025, announcement that the US Navy will build new nuclear-powered battleships; if the plan is realized, the ships could provide full-speed anti-aircraft and missile defense escort for US Navy carrier battle groups, and his decision could yet prove to have been prescient.
Trump also exercised leadership with his December 2017 decision to revive the US manned Moon Program, cancelled by his predecessor Barack Obama in April 2010, which gave China time to advance its manned lunar program to put Chinese on the Moon before or at about the same time as Americans return to the Moon.
The Trump Administration’s March 2026 decision to accelerate the US program to build Moon Bases — 79 space launches with four lunar habitats to be built by 2036 — provides a great opening for allied governments, the 70 current signatory states of the US-led Artemis Accords, and private space companies to contribute to or benefit from US and jointly developed technology.
The CCP will continue to invest heavily in the military, economic, and technological capabilities needed to expand its global influence. Democratic nations can respond by investing in the capabilities needed to preserve their own freedom of action — but doing so will require sustained commitments to defense, science, space infrastructure, and allied cooperation.
Richard D. Fisher, Jr., is a senior fellow with the International Assessment and Strategy Center.

Beware of China’s long-arm acts: MAC
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:10 UTC
01:43:10 KST

The Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) urged Taiwanese to exercise caution when considering trips to China after a Taiwanese man was allegedly questioned for six hours in Shanghai over past work with Amnesty International.
The council on Saturday said in a report that 426 Taiwanese have gone missing or been detained or had their freedom of movement restricted in China since Jan. 1, 2024.
The figure is up by seven from the previous week. New Chinese entry and exit regulations are due to take effect on Sept. 15, the council said.
Photo: Taipei Times
Of the 426 cases, 160 people have gone missing, up by five from the previous week; 36 have been detained for questioning, unchanged; and 230 are suspected of having had their freedom of movement restricted, an increase of two, it said.
Although the new regulations have not taken effect, major Chinese airports have reportedly begun subjecting outbound passengers to increased scrutiny.
The regulations would formalize existing control measures while leaving key definitions vague and subject to broad discretion, the MAC said.
Chinese authorities could apply the measures to Taiwanese travelers holding Taiwan compatriot permits, increasing the risks to their personal safety, it said.
There have been cases in which people who were once involved in political activities in Taiwan but later moved into non-political fields were still targeted by Chinese authorities and handed lengthy sentences over their past activities, the council said, urging Taiwanese not to take such risks lightly.
The council issued the remarks after a Taiwanese man said on social media that his son was allegedly stopped by Chinese customs while traveling to Shanghai on business and questioned for six hours by three plainclothes officials over alleged “political involvement.”
The son had worked for Amnesty International after graduating from university, the parent said.
The officials allegedly pressured him to unlock his cellphone and examined his messages, photographs, e-mails and work-related files and discussions on instant messaging apps. They questioned him about his responsibilities at the organization, its funding, his work on issues involving China, Hong Kong, Xinjiang and Tibet, and his contacts with political figures, human rights defenders and organizations, they said.
The parent said his son downplayed the political aspects of his former work, describing it as general administration, clerical work or academic research, emphasizing that he was not a decisionmaker or core advocate.
He eventually offered to withdraw his application to enter China and was able to return to Taiwan safely, they said.
The MAC said that although the person who made the social media post did not report the incident to the government, the experience described is consistent with similar cases previously documented by the authorities.
The parent appears to have shared what happened to raise public awareness of the risks of entering China, the council said, urging people to speak out and share their experiences to help inform the public.
Chinese authorities are hostile toward people affiliated with overseas nongovernmental organizations working on issues including human rights, environmental protection, government oversight, labor and gender diversity, it said.
The MAC urged people considered to be at high risk to carefully assess whether traveling to China is necessary.
The council said people who plan to travel to China should register using its registration system so authorities can provide assistance in an emergency.
When reached for comment, Tunghai University Center for China Studies deputy executive director Hung Pu-chao (洪浦釗) said the incident described by the parent should be taken seriously if verified.
“What China cares about is no longer simply who you are,” Hung said, adding that a person’s past involvement with sensitive issues, organizations and contacts could all become grounds for questioning at the border.
Taiwanese civil servants, police officers and judges have been subjected to questioning while traveling to China, he said.
If Chinese authorities can identify work experience that a person themselves has forgotten, it suggests that their access to information about Taiwanese extends deeply into their personal histories, he said.
Public resumes, social media activity, organizational records and information exposed in previous data breaches could all serve as potential sources, he said.
The government should compare such information with cases of Taiwanese being questioned in China to determine the scope and sources of the data held by Chinese authorities, he said.
A cellphone can contain information about family members, friends, colleagues and professional contacts, meaning that examining one person’s device could expose wider personal and professional networks, Hung said.
Taiwanese traveling to China should consider not only their personal safety, but also the security of data stored on their electronic devices, and take steps to protect personal and work-related information, he added.

Long-awaited Guangci/Fengtian Temple MRT Station opens in Taipei
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:08 UTC
01:43:08 KST

The Taipei MRT’s Guangci/Fengtian Temple Station opened yesterday, improving public transportation in eastern Xinyi District (信義) and potentially boosting local development after one of the city’s most challenging metro construction projects, authorities said.
Speaking at the inauguration ceremony, Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) said the 1.4km extension provides residents with a direct MRT connection to Tamsui (淡水) without requiring a transfer.
Chiang said the new station will provide an alternative to buses and help ease peak-hour congestion on Fude Street and Xinyi Road.
Photo: CNA
It would also allow passengers to travel directly to destinations including Taipei 101, Xiangshan (象山), Taipei Railway Station, National Taiwan University Hospital, Shilin (士林), Beitou (北投) and Tamsui without changing trains, he said.
The project posed major engineering challenges as the station was built beneath Fude Street, which is only 25m wide, Taipei’s Department of Rapid Transit Systems (DORTS) said.
Excavation reached a depth equivalent to about 10 stories, while heavy construction equipment at its closest point was only 60cm from nearby homes, requiring highly precise construction work, DORTS said.
The project also faced unusually difficult geological conditions. The shallow soil, which was once a wetland, was so soft that construction equipment could have sunk into it, it said.
More than 5,000 bags of cement were used to reinforce the ground before construction could proceed, it said.
Deeper underground, workers encountered bedrock that was about four times harder than expected, slowing the tunnel boring machine to a daily advance of just 2.5m, DORTS said.
Engineers ultimately adopted a series of modified construction methods to overcome the geological and site constraints and complete the project, it added.

Land policy should adapt to the aging society issue
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:08 UTC
01:43:08 KST

Property purchase-and-sale registrations accounted for just 57.9 percent of all building ownerships transfers last year, Ministry of the Interior data showed, the first time in a decade that the proportion has fallen below 60 percent. Inheritance transfers accounted for 17.4 percent, an all-time high, while gifts made up about 11.7 percent, a 10-year high.
The changes are partly attributable to 2023 amendments to the Equalization of Land Rights Act (平均地權條例) aimed at curbing speculation in the presale property market, as well as the implementation of the “integrated housing and land sales tax” and central bank credit controls in the housing market. Restrictions on loans for second homes and luxury properties, the cancelation of grace periods, and limited financing for land development and construction have all had a tangible impact on real-estate transactions, driving property investors out of the market.
However, the real underlying cause is Taiwan’s rapidly aging population.
Taiwan has entered the ranks of “super-aged” societies, with the number of deaths now exceeding the number of births each year. As the post-World War II baby-boom generation that acquired a lot of property ages, their assets are starting to be inherited, an irreversible demographic trend.
At the same time, housing prices have become so high that the average age of first-time homebuyers is already more than 40. Incomes have failed to keep pace with housing prices, leading to a decline in the number of property transactions.
With the aging population, government land administration agencies should adjust their functions accordingly.
First, they should provide a property inheritance advisory service. Land offices could establish one-stop service counters bringing together tax authorities, household registration offices, lawyers and land administration agents. They could provide advice on drafting wills, distributing estates, resolving co-ownership issues, gift planning and trusts.
Second, the government should identify land that has yet to be formally transferred to heirs, notify potential heirs, assist with inheritance cases involving people living overseas, enhance registration and monitoring systems, and accelerate public auctions of such properties to prevent land standing vacant.
Third, the government should establish a shared ownership negotiation platform to help parties access information and organize negotiations. Potential ownership plans could include an agreed partition of the property, having partial owners purchase the shares held by others, selling the land outright and distributing the proceeds, resolving the matter under Article 34 of the Land Act (土地法), or applying to a court for a judicial partition.
Fourth, they should establish maps of vacant, underused or long-unoccupied housing.
Fifth, social affairs, urban development, public works and health authorities should work together to develop housing policies specifically designed for an aging population.
As Taiwan’s population ages, land administration agencies should not resign themselves to operating merely as registration authorities. They should be remodeled as land governance and property succession centers, responsible for protecting people’s property rights, promoting the effective use of land, assisting older people with the transfer of their assets and supporting the needs of an aging society.
They could go even further by integrating themselves with urban renewal programs, housing policy and long-term care needs, creating institutions that reflect Taiwan’s changing demographics.
Chang Yao-jen is a former director of the Chiayi City Urban Development Office and an adjunct associate professor in Chinese Culture University’s Department of Land Resources.

Australia holds on to lead to put down Argentina
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:05 UTC
01:43:05 KST

Australia took their scoring chances and showed steel in defense, leading end to end to beat Argentina 27-21 Saturday in the first of two rugby Test matches.
Tries in the first 10 minutes by hooker Brandon Paenga-Amoso and flyhalf Carter Gordon gave Australia an early lead which it protected against an adventurous but less clinical Argentina.
Australia clung to their final six point margin for the last 27 minutes of the match when altitude-induced exhaustion at the mountainous venue saw sloppiness and imprecision leak into their game.
Photo: AFP
Their inability to retain possession, especially in the last 10 minutes, gave Argentina chances to snatch a win but the Australian defense rose to the occasion.
“Here at altitude the shoulders are sore, the lungs are sore,” said back Tom Hooper, who scored Australia’s only second half try. “It was a hard test match and the whole 23 got us across the line.”
Australia remains unbeaten in three matches under former rugby league star Les Kiss, who succeeded Joe Schmidt as head coach.
“I think the way Les communicates is very calming,” Hooper said. “He’s brought a really good mindset in terms of how we’re training and if you want to be world class, get good results and lift a bit of silverware you have to train world class.”
When it kicked out of hand Saturday, Australia mostly looked to touch to apply pressure through field position while Argentina kicked contestably and often won back kicked possession.
Australia was more clinical than Argentina in attack, taking 18 points from visits to the Pumas 22 in the first half to lead 22-14 at halftime. It was not until the second half that they strung together a large number of phases and carried the ball from depth to the goal line to create Hooper’s try in the 53rd minute.
Argentina took only seven points from incursions into Australia’s 22 in the first half but looked more dangerous when it attacked from depth, on the counter or from turnovers. It had a knack of finding weak shoulders in the Australian defense but their finishing lacked sharpness.
Boris Wenger and back Joaquin Moro were industrious and scored tries while fullback Geronimo Piscatelli was a constant attacking threat, scoring one try and missing two others.
After Australia’s two-try opening, Piscatelli scored in the 14th minute when flyhalf Santiago Carreras got wing Rodrigo Isgro through a gap to open up the defense.
Wallaby back Fraser McReight scored in a goal line scramble to make Australia’s lead 19-7 after 20 minutes. Moro scored for Argentina from a free kick after a five meter scrum after Australia had defended stoutly with 14 men, with Harry Potter in the sin bin.
A Ryan Lonergan penalty gave Australia an eight-point halftime margin.
Argentina started the second half strongly and Piscatelli twice went close to scoring, his second attempt disallowed for a forward pass. Wenger scored in the 51st minute to cut the lead to one point at 22-21.
The match became scrappy through the middle of the second half but Hooper’s first try in three years, from a linebreak by Hunter Paisami gave Australia the line it held until full time.

Semicon to put spotlight on CPO, silicon photonics
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:01 UTC
01:43:01 KST

Silicon photonics and copackaged optics (CPO), technologies seen as critical to meeting the surging bandwidth demands of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, would be among the main themes at the Semicon Taiwan trade show, which opens on Wednesday, event organizer SEMI said yesterday.
The forum runs until Friday at the Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center, with technical forums beginning today.
The event is expected to set a record in terms of the number of participants, SEMI said, projecting more than 1,300 exhibitors from 65 countries across 4,300 booths and more than 100,000 attendees.
Photo: CNA
Optical interconnects underpinning AI infrastructure would be one of the highlights, with contract chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co’s (TSMC, 台積電) compact universal photonics engine (COUPE) platform and the industry’s progress toward mass CPO production expected to draw attention, it said.
With AI chips, high-performance computing processors and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) demanding faster data transmission, conventional electrical interconnects are increasingly giving way to optical communications to boost AI data center efficiency, SEMI said.
The industry is moving beyond chip-level speeds to upgrading rack-to-rack links, as copper interconnects near their limits in bandwidth, power consumption and transmission distance, it said.
Silicon photonics, which uses optical rather than electrical signals, could cut power consumption and data transfer costs, making this a key year for large-scale deployment, SEMI said.
The technology can integrate photonic integrated circuits with electronic integrated circuits, while CPO technology enables optical engines and switches to be packaged together.
In AI and high-performance computing chip systems, advanced packaging technologies can also integrate graphics processing units, AI accelerators, application-specific integrated circuits and HBM, enabling optoelectronic integration with high bandwidth, low latency and low power consumption while overcoming limitations in bandwidth, power consumption and transmission performance.
TSMC has been expanding its COUPE platform and “COUPE on Substrate” CPO solution, with products entering production this year.
AI chip designer Nvidia Corp has partnered with TSMC on COUPE and begun shipping next-generation Spectrum-X switches using CPO technology, with production expected to ramp up in the second half of the year.
TrendForce Corp (集邦科技) in a report last month said Nvidia’s Spectrum-X shipments and Broadcom Inc’s initial deliveries of its 51.2-terabit Bailly CPO switch show that the technology has entered the mass production stage.
Taiwanese firms are also accelerating commercialization, with United Microelectronics Corp (聯電) completing its first mass-produced silicon photonics wafers at its Singapore fab with partner Silith Technology Pte Ltd, the report said.
GlobalWafers Co (環球晶圓) also said some products entered volume production earlier this year, the report added.
Hon Hai Precision Industry Co (鴻海精密) expects to begin CPO switch shipments in the third quarter, while affiliate ShunSin Technology Holdings Ltd (訊芯科技) said it has achieved mass production capability for 51.2-terabit and 102.4-terabit CPO products through a collaboration with TSMC.
Powertech Technology Inc (力成科技), which is partnering with Broadcom Inc, plans to begin low-volume production for optical engine components this year before integrating them into CPO switches next year.
Largan Precision Co (大立光) is preparing for a trial production of its first automated CPO line after securing a fiber-array order.
Testing suppliers are expanding, too, with Materials Analysis Technology Inc (閎康科技) installing advanced silicon photonics testing equipment, and ASE Technology Holding Co (日月光投控) building out its CPO ecosystem through subsidiaries and its VIPack packaging platform, the report said.
AM Intelligence, an Indian artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure company, has ordered 9,000 Nvidia Corp Vera Rubin systems, seeking to become one of the first adopters of the advanced computing platform in Asia. Servers equipped with the rack-scale systems are slated to come online next year in southern India, the Hyderabad-based company said in a statement yesterday. Customers include major cloud service providers, AI labs and organizations aiming to develop homegrown Indian AI models, it said. Supplies of high-end Nvidia compute clusters remain tight. Demand from data centers and companies such as Microsoft Corp, Alphabet Inc’s Google and Amazon.com Inc to train AI models

Fuel prices to stay steady for the fifth consecutive week
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-30
16:43:00 UTC
01:43:00 KST

CPC Corp, Taiwan (CPC, 台灣中油) on Saturday announced that it would leave domestic gasoline and diesel prices unchanged this week, with Formosa Petrochemical Corp (台塑石化) yesterday saying it would do the same.
It is the fifth consecutive week that CPC and Formosa have kept domestic crude oil prices steady under the government’s price stabilization measures.
Retail gasoline prices this week remain at NT$30.5, NT$32 and NT$34 per liter for 92, 95 and 98-octane unleaded gasoline respectively at CPC and Formosa stations.
Prices of premium diesel would stay at NT$29.3 per liter at CPC stations and NT$29.1 per liter at Formosa pumps, they said.
International crude oil prices last week ended lower despite apparent stalling in diplomatic efforts to end the war between the US and Iran, and a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remaining uncertain.
CPC said its floating price mechanism, based on a weighted average of 70 percent Dubai and 30 percent Brent crude, showed that the average international crude oil price fell to US$91.56 last week from US$93.01 per barrel in the week before.
Additionally, a stronger New Taiwan dollar against the US dollar reduced purchasing costs, it said.
CPC said that as of yesterday, it has absorbed an estimated NT$18.03 billion (US$570.06 million) in losses since the war in the Middle East started in February, by not fully passing on higher international crude oil costs on to consumers and businesses to ease domestic inflationary pressure.
